## BUG-052

**Command / Area:** PIT BLOCK 3 — force-adoption + elimination of PIT BLOCK 2 across the suite. PIT/IO/OF/etc. inserts, drawing-open behaviour, installer payload.

**Symptom (Tim, 2026-06-12):** "Why are we on v2.1.3 and still not force-using PIT BLOCK 3? Why hasn't it shipped? How does it get rid of all use of PIT BLOCK 2?"

**Root cause found:**
1. **PIT BLOCK 3.dwg was never in the running bundle.** `DeployToDevBundle` (the dev workflow) copies only the DLL/assets/icons/runtimes — NOT block `.dwg` files. Blocks ship only via the installer EXE, and no EXE has been built since PB3 was added to `source_blocks` on 9 Jun. The bundle's `Contents\Blocks\` was frozen at an old install (only `PIT BLOCK 2.dwg`, dated 4 Feb). So the code's "prefer PB3" preference could never find the file → silently fell back to PB2.
2. **Current design is PREFERENCE, not FORCE.** New pits prefer PB3; old drawings keep PB2/PB until someone manually runs `CDREFRESHBLOCKS`. Nothing auto-forces.
3. **PB2 is deliberately KEPT** (recognised, 2nd variant, shipped) — by design it coexists, it does not get eliminated.

**Tim's decisions (2026-06-12):** FULL FORCE + ELIMINATE PB2; deliver via FULL INSTALLER EXE for the office.

**DONE this session (safe, immediate):**
- `DeployToDevBundle` now syncs `Installer\source_blocks\*.dwg` → bundle `Contents\Blocks` every dev build (root-cause fix so blocks never go missing again).
- Copied `PIT BLOCK 3.dwg` into the running bundle NOW → new pits resolve PB3 immediately (Tim can verify: place a pit → Properties reads "PIT BLOCK 3").

**REMAINING (force + eliminate) — gated on AC-closed + Tim's one real-drawing test before office EXE:**
- **Auto-redefine on drawing open:** wire the `CDREFRESHBLOCKS` redefine (`db.Insert(name, PB3sourceDb, true)`) to run once-per-database on open/first-CE-touch (reuse the hardened once-per-db `EnsureDrawingDiscovered` hook + CommandInProgress guard — DO NOT add a new DocumentActivated reactor; this is the recurring-regression zone, see memory regression_dbtext_dtext_doubleclick). Redefines in-drawing PB/PB2 defs from PB3.dwg → all existing pits show PB3 geometry automatically.
- **Eliminate the PB2 NAME (destructive):** reassign every pit BlockReference from "PIT BLOCK 2"/"PIT BLOCK" to the "PIT BLOCK 3" definition (preserve dynamic props: SPS_RADIUS, X/Y width, visibility states), then purge the PB2/PB defs so Properties reads "PIT BLOCK 3" everywhere. PRECONDITION: verify PB2↔PB3 dynamic-property names are identical (PB3 was built from PB2 — likely safe, but MUST confirm or pits break — the 2026-06-09 note warned of exactly this). Drop PB2 from `GetBlockNameVariants`, remove `PIT BLOCK 2.dwg` from `source_blocks`, keep recognition ONLY for the in-session migration pass.
- **Verify:** unit tests (variant order now `["PIT BLOCK 3","PIT BLOCK"]`; every-recognition-site test) + headless redefine/reassign round-trip (isolated accoreconsole, runs with AC open).
- **Ship:** close AC → build net48+net10 (DLL now carries blocks) → bump 2.1.4 → build installer EXE → Tim test: open an OLD PB2 job → all pits read "PIT BLOCK 3", SPS grip works, PITSCHEDULE/CDEDIT fine, nothing lost → THEN distribute EXE.

**Update 2026-06-12 (code complete, headless-proven):** `PitBlockMigrationService` built (pure
planner + apply + auto-on-open trigger + CDREFRESHBLOCKS wiring). PB2↔PB3 confirmed structurally
identical (15 ents, 0 attrs) so redefine + RENAME (handle-preserving) is safe — no reference swap,
CE link graph intact. Tests: 8 planner + 3 wiring + headless T3 (7/7 incl. handle preserved, name→PB3,
still recognised). Full suite 1918/1944. Residual v1 limits: mixed PB2+PB3 drawings keep a few PB2
names (geometry uniform); PB2.dwg still shipped/recognised for un-migrated drawings (final cleanup
gated on rollout). REMAINING: Tim closes AC → deploy v2.1.4 (DLL now carries blocks) → build office
EXE → Tim runs the 5-step AC test in REGRESSION_LOG → distribute.

**Status:** IN PROGRESS — code + tests + headless DONE 2026-06-12; gated on AC-closed deploy + Tim's real-drawing test before office EXE.

## BUG-098

**Command / Area:** pit labels vs stored pit identity (plan label text, CDINSPECTOR, long section, schedule).

**Symptom (Tim, 2026-09-14 09:40 AEST, live bundle fc42544a):** the plan shows pit labels P10 and P9 on a 2 × 100 UPVC detention pair; CDINSPECTOR on the pit labelled P10 reports ID **P8** with "→ 100 UPVC to P9"; the long section drawn afterwards is headed P9 → P8 (follows the record). CDDASHBOARD reports no issue. The section was drawn after the labels were already in this state.

**Expected:** the label text on the plan, the stored pit ID, the section header and the schedule all say the same pit number; a mismatch must be flagged as Unknown/needs attention by the automatic QA, not silently accepted.

**Root cause:** not yet established. Candidates: a renumber that updated the record but not the label attribute (or the reverse), or a hand-edited label. Evidence to gather: `CDINSPECTOR` on the pit labelled P9 (does it say P9 or P7?), the pit schedule rows, and whether the labels were typed by hand or produced by a CE renumber.

**Triage 29 Sep (release chat 04): fix found in code, 813b4672 / 4a79f5ee (pit label mismatch warning), present in the installed Civil 3.0.13. Status stays open until a Codex/Tim check confirms it in AutoCAD; queued for Codex pass 18.**

## BUG-101

**Command / Area:** CDSTRIP Accept (atomic read-back of the fall-arrow Leaders); vertex prompt wording; preview wording.

**Symptom:** typed `A` at the preview → `[CE] A staged fall arrow differs from the accepted plan.` — nothing drawn. `Next point [Undo] [Undo]`. `Preview: … Zero justification` after choosing Center.

**Root cause:** AutoCAD hides a Leader arrowhead when the shaft is shorter than 2 × Dimasz × Dimscale (= 600 mm for TIM LEADER); the shaft was exactly 600 and rounds to 599.999… in most directions (measured in accoreconsole 2027: 599 no head, 600/601 head). The atomic read-back saw `HasArrowHead == false` and refused. The old route drew those arrows headless silently.

**Status:** FIXED IN SOURCE — 2026-09-14 (REGRESSION_LOG BUG-101): shaft 610 mm, every-degree guard test, prompt/wording fixes, specific read-back message. Awaiting Tim's AutoCAD retest.

## BUG-495

**Command / Area:** COLLEAGUE RELEASE GATE CANDIDATE. HUNT2-S-01 (HIGH): Publish Issue (CESHEETS > Publish Issue, and the Sheets Manager window) gives the typed revision and the issue date to EVERY Structural sheet in the job, including sheets the drafter left out of this issue. What the drafter sees: a 10-sheet set where only S03 and S05 changed comes out with all ten at revision C, dated today. Eight sheets that did not change now claim a change; a builder holding revision B of S07 is told it is superseded when it is not. Sheets left out of the issue also jump to C in the sheet list without ever being issued. Evidence (reading only): UI/Dialogs/CeSheetsWindow.xaml.cs 263-273 (called at 492) writes the revision onto every Structural sheet; SheetsOfDiscipline 206-212 ignores the tick 'include in issue'; Services/CeSheetsIssueService.cs 24-32 and 86-109 date every sheet when no ticked list is given; CeSheetsManagerWindow.xaml.cs 1191-1196 does the same. The ticked-sheets route exists (CeSheetsIssueService.cs 39-47) and so does the issue preview (Services/CeIssuePreviewBuilder.cs) but NO window calls either; the Settings switch IssuePreviewEnabled (Models/UserSettings.cs 268-271) is read by nothing. The Publish Issue window also refuses a blank revision (CeIssuePublishDialog.xaml.cs 198-200) against INT-059 item 22. It breaks Tim's 14 Sep ruling (card 04_REFERENCE/structural/cards/STRUC-REGISTER-ISSUE_CARD_2026-09-26.md section 4): 'Unchanged sheets keep their existing revision and date, a set-wide issue date must never overwrite them' and 'Before plotting, show an issue preview'. Related but different: BUG-398 (preview engine disagreeing for unticked sheets). Right result: only the ticked sheets get the new revision and date, and the issue preview is shown before anything plots. Smallest fix: make both windows use the ticked-sheets route and show the preview first. To SEE it: a job copy with three Structural sheets at revision B; CESHEETS, untick 'include' on sheet 3, Publish Issue, Structural, revision C. Wrong: sheets 1 and 2 at C dated today and sheet 3 also at C in the list. Right: sheet 3 stays at B. **Command / Area:** HUNT2-S-04 (MEDIUM-HIGH): STRSCHEDREFRESH never removes rows, so a brace or pier that was erased stays on the schedule. What the drafter sees: four braces drawn, one erased, STRSCHEDREFRESH and pick the bracing schedule: it still lists four braces, the last row being the old fourth one. ## BUG-505

**Command / Area:** COLLEAGUE RELEASE GATE CANDIDATE. HUNT2-C-01 (HIGH): the X-Civil and LandXML imports never read the source drawing's UNITS, so a millimetre job can come in 1000 times too big, silently. What the drafter sees: CDIMPORTXCIVIL on a millimetre X-Civil drawing puts the pits and pipes 1000 times further from the origin than the X-Civil linework, and 1000 times too big, with no line on the command line saying CE changed the scale. The same happens for any X-Civil or LandXML import into a drawing whose UNITS are Metres. A wrong scale on a whole job is the risk: every pit position and size on the drawing is wrong, and nothing warns the drafter. Evidence (reading only): Services/XcivilEntityScanner.cs 427-486 guesses whether the X-Civil drawing is in metres and stops at the FIRST thing that looks metre-sized (one pit block 0.05 to 3.0 wide, 436-442, or one polyline on a pipe layer 1 to 250 long, 448-455), although the comment says 'if EVERY named pit'. Then every position, pit size and pipe diameter is multiplied by 1000 (499-518, called at Services/XcivilImportService.cs 323-325); the scale goes only to the debug file (324). Neither this route nor the LandXML route (Helpers/LandXmlParser.cs 170-173) looks at the CURRENT drawing's UNITS: both always place in millimetres. The downpipe symbol reader does use the drawing's UNITS (Services/BackgroundDownpipeSymbolReader.cs 73-77). I think a 200 mm stub, a short leader or a short tail of pipe linework on a pipe layer is common in a millimetre drawing, so a real job can trip this. Right result: CE reads the X-Civil drawing's UNITS and the target drawing's UNITS, scales between them, and says so in one line ('X-Civil drawing is in metres; placed in this millimetre drawing at 1000 times'); where the units are not set it asks once. Smallest fix: use both drawings' Insunits (the same DrawingAreaUnits.MillimetresPerUnit the downpipe reader uses); keep the guess only when UNITS are not set, require most pits to agree, and print the scale used. No test today for the scale guess. To SEE it: take a COPY of a millimetre X-Civil drawing that imports correctly today, add one 200 mm polyline on its pipe layer, save; CDIMPORTXCIVIL into a copy of a job drawing; ZOOM Extents. Wrong: everything 1000 times out. Then set UNITS to Metres in a copy of the target drawing and import again. Right: a one-line scale message and the job in the right place. ## BUG-506

**Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-02 (MEDIUM): the CDDESIGN calculation summary prints the connection pipe grade as '1:0'. Right result: 'Grade 1:100' (the N the sizer gave). Smallest fix: print '1:' + N without dividing, and change the report test to feed 100. To SEE it: a copy of a job with a council and areas set; CDDESIGN, work the design out, read CONNECTION PIPE in the summary. Wrong: Grade 1:0. Right: Grade 1:100. Right result: all flows on the job's curve, or a line saying which curve each figure used. To SEE it: a copy of a job; CDRAINFALL, set the job's own coefficients; CDDESIGN, read Q minor and Q major; compare with the same figures worked by hand from the job's curve. Wrong: they match the office curve. Right: they match the job's curve. **Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-10 (MEDIUM): CDRULES adds a 'Velocity uses Assumed roughness' warning for every pipe, even after Tim confirms the roughness. What the drafter sees: CDRULES gives one warning per pipe saying the velocity uses an assumed roughness, also after the Manning n values are confirmed in Settings. **Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-11 (MEDIUM): the Boyd's storage can be too small when the worst storm is longer than the last row, and nothing says so. What the reviewer sees: CDCALC's Boyd's tab works only 5 to 30 minute storms; CDDESIGN works 5 to 180 minutes. A wrong number on a design is the risk: an undersized tank looks like a finished answer, and the two tools disagree for one site (design rule #1). Evidence (reading only): ViewModels/BoydsCalcViewModel.cs 87-92 (six rows, 5 to 30 min) and 189-211 (largest row wins); Services/DetentionSizingService.cs 66-67 (fixed list ending 180) and 131-158 (largest row wins). Neither checks whether the largest is the last row. I think on a normal house lot the worst storm is 30 to 120 minutes, so CDCALC's 30-minute limit is the one most likely to bite. No test for the last-row case. Right result: both use the same storm list, and when the worst storm is the last one CE says 'storage still rising at 180 minutes: add longer storms before issuing'. Smallest fix: a one-line check after each sweep, and one shared storm list (a Settings value). To SEE it: a copy of a job; CDCALC Boyd's with a small permitted discharge (for example 2 L/s on 700 m2); read the critical duration; CDDESIGN on the same figures and compare the storage. Wrong: a storage with no warning at the last row, and two different storages. Right: a warning, and one storage. ## BUG-521

**Command / Area:** HUNT3 5.1 (MEDIUM, ENGINEERING-RESULT RISK): the minimum pipe cover is read from two places that can disagree on the same pit. CDRULES uses council, then project, then office; the CE Inspector (network summary and pit cover row) and the Design Check Dashboard and repair checks use the office value only. A wrong answer on a design check is the risk: the same pit can pass in the Inspector and be a warning in CDRULES, or the other way round, and a drafter who trusts the Inspector can issue a pipe that is too shallow for the council. Example: a council job with a 450 mm council minimum and the office 300 mm: a pit with 350 mm cover is OK in the Inspector and a warning in CDRULES. The in-code fall-back is also 600 mm while the Settings default is 300 mm, so a blank value gives a third answer. Same kind as BUG-255 (Edit Pipe size strip uses a fixed 600 mm cover), in other places. Evidence (reading only): CDRULES Modules/Drainage/Rules/RulebookValues.cs 210-220 (council > project > office); Services/InspectorPaletteService.cs 2335 and 3036, Services/LinkService.RepairAudit.Analysis.cs 191 and 251 all read DesignStandards.MinimumCoverDepth and fall back to 600 mm; Settings default 300 mm at Models/UserSettings.cs 1174. No test covers the three sources together. Right result: every place that judges cover asks the same reader and gets the council value first. Smallest fix: make the four places read the resolved rulebook value (the BUG-255 cure applied here too). To SEE it: on a copy, give a job a council minimum cover of 450 mm and the office 300 mm; put a pit at 350 mm cover; read the Inspector, the Design Check Dashboard and CDRULES. Wrong: Inspector OK, CDRULES warning. Right: all three say warning at 450 mm. Related: the pipe speed limit has the same split (BUG-527). ## BUG-522

**Command / Area:** HUNT3 6.1 (LOW): nothing at start-up notices two different copies of CE_SHARED. Civil and Manager must ship byte-identical CE_SHARED because AutoCAD loads whichever copy comes first and the other plugin silently uses it. What could happen: a PC with a half-finished update (see BUG-478) has Civil from one release and Manager from another; AutoCAD uses the first loaded copy and nothing says so, so a button or window can behave as the older release. The hunt checked today's installed bundles and they are clean (byte-identical CE_SHARED.dll in all three lanes, all dated 9 Oct 08:35-08:36), so this is a guard that is missing, not a fault on Tim's PC today. Evidence (reading only): Shared/CE_SHARED/CE_SHARED.csproj 15 gives AssemblyVersion 1.1.0.0, fixed, so the version number never tells two copies apart; no start-up check in Civil or Manager compares the CE_SHARED AutoCAD actually loaded with the one in the plugin's own bundle. A Manager release build does refuse a CE_SHARED that is not the approved Civil one (Modules/Manager/CE_SUITE_MANAGER.csproj 175-216, pair approval at Services/CeApprovedReleaseService.cs 136), but that guard does not run on a colleague's PC. Right result: Civil and Manager compare the loaded file with their own copy at start and print one plain line if they differ. **Command / Area:** HUNT3 heading 5, findings 5.2 to 5.4 (one Settings value read from two places that can disagree; grouped; severity kept per item; the cover split is BUG-521). (5.2, MEDIUM, ENGINEERING-RESULT RISK) pipe speed limit: the CE Inspector and the Design Check Dashboard judge speed against the office maximum (or 3.0 m/s when blank) while CDRULES judges it against the per-material scour figures, so one pipe can be OK in the Inspector and a warning in CDRULES, and a wrong answer on a design check is the risk. (5.3, LOW) fall-back numbers in code that differ from the Settings default; I think they only bite when a Settings group is missing or blank in the file, so rarely: concrete joint label height 150 in code (Commands/CdJointCommand.cs 116, 151, 172) against 250 in Settings (UserSettings.cs 1431, 1434); text offset 0 or 400 (CdCommand.cs 677, 964, CdCommand.SamePlanBreak.cs 397, Services/PipeCreationService.cs 292, Services/XcivilPipeInsertionService.cs 148, Services/LinkService.CloneRegeneration.cs 139) against 70 (UserSettings.cs 796); invert mask gap 0 (Services/TextService.cs 67) against 70 (621); longest pipe run 0 (Services/LinkService.FlatPipeRepair.cs 37) against 80 m (UserSettings.cs 1254); fix: take every fall-back from the Settings model's own default, one number per value. (5.4, MEDIUM, I think visible, not seen) the job timer is set in two files and Civil and Structural each run their own timer in every drawing: Civil CD_Settings.json jobTime (user name, idle minutes 5, auto resume, data folder, status-bar timer; Models/UserSettings.cs 154-177) and Structural CS_Settings.json General (the same five; Modules/Structural/Models/UserSettings.cs 218-236, labelled 'Pause timer after (minutes)' and 'Show status bar timer' at Services/SettingsService.LoadRecovery.cs 1269, 1273); both start a timer at load with no check for the other (Modules/Drainage/Services/CivilJobTimeService.cs 28; Modules/Structural/Services/CeToolsInitializer.cs 63); Civil finds and saves its own time-log folder (Services/CivilJobTimeSettings.cs 76-90); I think a drafter who changes 'Pause timer after' in Structural still gets Civil pausing at 5 minutes, two status-bar timers may show, and the two time logs can land in different folders, which would split a job's hours between two files; fix: one owner for the timer and its five values (Tim's INT-076 item 2, naming by user, stays). To SEE 5.2: on a copy, a pipe running at 4.5 m/s in a material whose scour figure is 3.5 m/s; Inspector versus CDRULES. The one Settings value for it, Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm = 2.5 (Modules/Structural/Models/UserSettings.cs 1628), is read by only two commands: Services/ReoBarService.cs 936 and Services/ScheduleService.cs 135, 157. Examples of the other places: Commands/RebarCommands.cs 91, 93, 210, 325, 472; Services/FoundationService.cs 5071, 5140 (footing labels; 250 when DIMSCALE is not set, from the constant at line 37); Commands/ColumnDetailCommands.cs 19; Commands/SectionDetailCommands.cs 19; Commands/SbeamCommandRunner.cs 15. Item 25: tie-down, pump pit, bored pier and subfloor labels are a fixed 100 drawing units and ignore DIMSCALE: Services/TieDownService.cs 66, Services/PumpPitService.cs 243, Services/BoredPierPlacementService.cs 402, Services/TimberSubfloorService.cs 336, 362. I think that at 1:100 that prints about 1 mm high, against the 2.5 mm rule elsewhere; nobody has looked at one on paper. Item 21: beam labels are a fixed 250 (main) and 180 (suffix, colour 6), not scaled by DIMSCALE: Services/BeamDraftingStandards.cs 96, 99, 102, 108, used for the CANT, CONT, LOWER suffixes in Services/BeamService.cs 570-578. The code says 'do not change without consulting Tim', so any change needs Tim's word. A wrong size on paper is the risk: a label too small to read on a printed plan, or text that differs between commands on one drawing. Right result: every label reads one Settings value (the existing Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm, shown on the Settings page as 'Label height on paper (mm)'), with beam main and suffix heights as their own Text sizes boxes (proposed TextSizes.BeamLabelMm, TextSizes.BeamSuffixMm). Smallest fix: one shared helper that returns the label height from the Settings value and DIMSCALE, used by all 23 places; then the beam heights as two boxes. To SEE it: place a tie-down, a pump pit and a bored pier label at 1:100, plot or measure the text height on paper and compare with a footing label (right: both 2.5 mm); change Label plot height on the Settings page and see which commands follow (today only reo bars and the schedules). ## BUG-532

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC items 28 and 29 (MEDIUM; layer names written into the code, and four objects drawn on two different layer names). What the drafter sees: the same kind of object lands on a different layer depending on which command drew it, so a footing plan's layers split between commands and drafters. The four cases: (1) bored piers: BP uses 'BORED PIER' (Modules/Structural/Services/FoundationService.cs 2013) but the layer map, the native pier tool and the bored pier plan use 'BORED PIER UNDER' (Services/LayerService.cs 94, Services/NativeBoredPierService.cs 14, Models/UserSettings.cs 1583). (2) joists: 'JOISTS' (Commands/RafterJoistCommands.cs 21) against 'FLOOR JOISTS' (Models/UserSettings.cs 1257). (3) stump footings: 'STUMP FOOTING' (Services/FoundationStumpFootingService.cs 14) against 'BORED PIER UNDER' in the layer map (Services/LayerService.cs 97). (4) pads and strips both go on 'STRIP FOOTINGS' (Services/LayerService.cs 95-96). Behind it: Services/LayerService.cs 87-118 maps each kind of object to a layer name written in the code (BEAM, BEAM LOWER, LOADBEARING WALL, WALL BRACING TYPE A and B, SUPPORT COLUMN, SUPPORT DS, BORED PIER UNDER, STRIP FOOTINGS, SLAB INTERNAL BEAM, 35CONT, 25DIMS, 25TEXT, BATTER, GUIDELINES and the rest), and there are 63 more named layer constants in 30 files (for example Commands/RafterJoistCommands.cs 20-24, Services/TieDownService.cs 27, Services/TimberSubfloorService.cs 48-58, Services/FoundationService.cs 21-25). Colours and linetypes are taken by name from the office template drawing (LayerService.cs 540); the names themselves are not on the Settings page, except for the few groups that carry their own layer (roof and floor setout, lintels, level carry, framing legend, bored pier plan, basement, pump pit, reo bars, foundation plan, weld mark). Not a wrong number, but a wrong layer on paper is the risk: an object plotted with the wrong line weight or frozen with the wrong layer. Right result: one layer name per kind of object, held on the Settings page (proposed Layers.<Kind>, Layers tab, labels such as 'Layer for beams'), read by every command that draws that object, so a pier is on the same layer whichever command drew it. Smallest fix: first make the four double-ups agree (Tim to say which layer name is right for each), then move the layer map onto the Settings page. To SEE it: draw a bored pier with BP and another with the bored pier plan tool and check the layer of each in the Layer Properties palette (today: BORED PIER and BORED PIER UNDER); repeat with joists and a stump footing. ## BUG-533

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC item 31 (and item 41) (MEDIUM; the required bracing lengths are stored on the PC, not with the job; same fault as BUG-500, and the same cause as BUG-496, the job record kept per PC). What the drafter sees: the North-South and East-West required bracing figures (CSBRACINGREQUIRED, typed in the bracing panel) are one value for the whole PC. The code's own comment says 'entered once per job', but it is stored in the PC's settings, so the last job's figure sits on the next job and a colleague opening the same drawing does not see it. Evidence: Modules/Structural/Models/UserSettings.cs 705-706 (the two values, empty by default so no number is invented); Commands/BracingPanelCommands.cs 95-125 (where they are typed in). Item 41 for the record: CE holds no bracing capacities or factors at all. Structural.DesignCore/BracingPanelCalculator.cs only adds up brace lengths against the required length the drafter types, and Models/UserSettings.cs 700-704 says there is no AS 1684 bracing table. Nothing to move to Settings there. A wrong number on a design is the risk: a bracing panel showing '/ 12000 mm required' with a tick or a cross against another job's requirement. Right result: the required bracing is a job value held with the job record, shown under Bracing as 'Required bracing for this job (mm)', and an empty value reads as Unknown. Smallest fix: do this together with BUG-500 and BUG-496 (one job-record fix covers all three); do not fix it separately. To SEE it: set the required bracing on job A, open job B and see job A's figure on the bracing panel (today: it shows); on a second PC open job A and see no figure. ## BUG-534

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC items 14, 15, 19, 32, 33, 40 (MEDIUM-HIGH; five standards tables that must be cited with their editions, in the tables and in the output; plus items 11, 39, 49 and 50 that lean on a standard without citing it). The five: (1) AS 3600 cover: UI/Dialogs/RCMemberDialog.xaml.cs 194-202 (Modules/Structural), under 20 red, under 25 amber, under 30 a note; the code's own comment calls it 'Simplified' and names exposure A1, A2 and B1; it ignores concrete strength. (2) AS 3600 bar spacing: RCMemberDialog.xaml.cs 207-208 (clear gap at least the bar size or 25, aggregate assumed 20 or less) and 245 (centres over 300 give a 'crack control' caution), citing Cl 8.1.7.1 and Cl 8.6.1. (3) AS/NZS 4671 bar table with AS 3600 laps: Assets/Config/rebar-catalogue.json (names AS/NZS 4671 and 'AS3600-2018 Table 13.2.2 (f'c=32MPa, Class N bar, standard hook)'); the laps and covers in it are read by no command, only the diameters are; a fallback copy is at Services/ReinforcementService.cs 110-120 and a second, separate bar table at Services/StandardsService.cs 78-86 feeds the RBL, RBC and STR bar size question. (4) AS 2870 founding note wording: Models/UserSettings.cs 87-91 (FoundingNote.Template, in the file only, no box on CESETTINGS). (5) AS 1684.2: the timber subfloor starter span table (100x50 at 1200, 150x50 at 1800, 200x50 at 2400) at Models/UserSettings.cs 1439-1469; the code's own comment says it is NOT checked against AS 1684.2. Also AS 4055: the wind class steps and the N1-N6 / C1-C4 ladder (Models/UserSettings.cs 111-128, Rules/WindClassSuggestion.cs 14-15) are an office simplification of AS 4055 with no citation. Lean on a standard without citing: lig hook shapes (Services/StructuralDetailService.cs 433-437, item 39, I think AS 3600 hook rules); the steel section spelling table (Services/ExcelMTextService.cs 246-338, item 11, a catalogue list, cite its source); checklist live loads '3.0kPa Office / 5.0kPa Public Assembly' (Core/Checklist/TemplateManager.cs 949, 1057, 1110, AS/NZS 1170.1, item 49); the AS 2870 site class list (Rules/GeotechReport.cs 50, item 50). A wrong number on a design or on paper is the risk: a cover or span from a table with no edition behind it can be out of date or for a different exposure or strength, and the output gives the reader no way to tell. Right result: each table is on the Settings page (proposed Concrete.CoverTable, Concrete.BarTable, Wind and soil tab) showing its standard and edition, the output (the beam window messages, the founding note, the schedules) names the same edition, and the 1684.2 span table is replaced by cited figures before any job uses it. Smallest fix: first add the standard and edition beside each table and in each printed note; the full cover table by exposure and strength is a second step (Tim to rule on editions). To SEE it: open RCBEAM, enter cover 22 and read the colour and message (today: amber, 'Simplified' check, no standard or edition named); look at the Timber subfloor tab and the founding note on a general notes sheet for any edition. ## BUG-536

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC items 5, 7, 20, 23, 24, 26, 27 and 34 (MEDIUM; EIGHT commands that ignore a Settings name that already exists, or read it for only part of the job). What the drafter sees: they change a value on the Settings page (or in the file) and the command carries on with its own built-in number. The eight, all under Modules/Structural: (1) SCREWPILE: offers 300 (Services/FoundationScrewPileService.cs 172) while FootingWidth.ScrewPileDiameterMm is 150 (Models/UserSettings.cs 1115, fallback Services/FoundationService.cs 28), so a pile redrawn without a size is 150 and a new one is offered 300; the two numbers disagree. (2) BP (bored pier): offers [300/450/600] <450> (Services/FoundationService.cs 1981-1992) and ignores BoredPierPlan.DefaultDiameterMm = 450 (Models/UserSettings.cs 1567); always uses block 450DIABPV2 (2012-2013); the hatched version is offered only for 450 (1998). (3) REBAR / RB: starts at N12, 200 mm, 3 bars (Services/NativeTimToolsService.cs 31-35) and ignores Rebar.DefaultSize and Rebar.DefaultSpacing (N12 / 200, on the Settings page). (4) Beam shorten: the two choices 45 and 100 are fixed (Commands/BeamPlacementCommands.cs 1426-1437); only the last pick is remembered in Beams.LastShortenDistance (in the file only). (5) Every label command: Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm is read by two commands of 25 (see BUG-531). (6) Member schedule (XCLMTXT / EXCELMTEXT): row and text sizes are built in at Services/ExcelMTextService.cs 37-53 and 4091-4094 (mark text 300, description 200, row 750, boxes 1450 and 4700 wide, column set 6950, bands 750); only Excel.RowsPerColumn 31, Excel.FloorSectionGap 3000 and the text offsets are on the page. They must match the office MEMBER SCHEDULE block. (7) Footing schedule: text 250, row 350, 1:100 when no scale is set (Services/ScheduleService.cs 36-38) and column widths 3600 and 1800 (Services/FoundationScheduleService.cs 32-33); the sizes follow Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm but the widths do not follow any Settings value. (8) CSLOADPATH: Models/UserSettings.cs 1315-1321 holds LoadPath.AssumedPointLoadKN (20), .AssumedAllowableBearingKPa (100), .MinPadSizeMm (450) in the file only, and the round-up to the next 50 mm (Structural.DesignCore/LoadPathEngine.cs 214) and a pier with no size counted as 450 (LoadPathEngine.cs 141) are built in. A wrong number on paper is the risk: the drafter believes the Settings value is in force and the pile size, the pad offered or the schedule sizing on the sheet come from a different built-in number. Right result: each of the eight reads its Settings name (adding the missing names, for example Rebar.DefaultBarCount, Beams.ShortenChoicesMm, BoredPierPlan.DiameterChoicesMm, FootingSchedule.ColumnWidths, MemberSchedule.TextHeights, .RowHeight, .ColumnWidths, LoadPath.PadRoundUpMm), and the two pile numbers become one. Smallest fix: wire the existing names first (REBAR, BP, SCREWPILE), then add the missing names. To SEE it: change Rebar default size to N16 on CESETTINGS and run REBAR (today: still N12); change the bored pier plan diameter and run BP (today: still 450); run SCREWPILE and compare the offered size with the size drawn for a pile without one. ## BUG-538

**Command / Area:** R00_CIVIL items 4 (the council and rising-main parts), 5 and 6 (MEDIUM-HIGH; council rules written into the code, so a council change needs a new build of the plugin). What the drafter sees: CDDESIGN gives a storage or a pump result that follows rules the plugin carries inside itself, not the council profile and not the Settings page. If a council changes its rule, nothing changes until a new plugin build, and the drafter cannot see or correct the number. The values, each with file:line: (1) Bayside: the pump station storm is forced to 1 in 20 (Services/PumpSizingService.cs 125, applied at 303-306 as the audit gives it); (2) rising main size: 50 mm up to 5 L/s, otherwise 80 mm (Services/PumpSizingService.cs 98, 101, 104; the audit calls this an office habit, not a named council rule, and it has no Settings name); (3) Kingston: a 500 L credit for each 2000 L block of reuse (Services/ReuseCreditService.cs 31-34, 75, 78); (4) Manningham: a factor of 0.25, applying only with at least 2000 L of reuse and 50 m2 of roof (same file, same lines); (5) Casey: a reuse credit of one-third (same file); (6) Casey orifice formula constant K 21.9 (Services/OrificeSizer.cs 55, used by CDDESIGN at Services/AutoDesignService.cs 409 when the Casey profile has no orificeFormulaK; the council field exists, but the code keeps its own copy as the fallback; the audit marks this item 'partly'). The reuse credits reach the CDDESIGN storage result (Services/AutoDesignOrchestrator.cs 154) and the pump rules reach the CDDESIGN pump result (Services/AutoDesignOrchestrator.cs 173). The reuse rules are not in Assets/Config/council-profiles.json at all. A wrong council number on a design is the risk: a storage or a pump sized on an out-of-date council rule, with nothing on the sheet to show the number came from the plugin and not from the council. Right result: council rules live in the council profile / Settings page, each with the source and the edition named, so a council change is a Settings edit and not a new build (proposed council profile fields reuseCreditRule, reuseBlockL, reuseCreditPerBlockL, reuseFactor, reuseMinL, reuseMinRoofM2 shown on the council page under 'Rainwater reuse credit'; the Bayside 1 in 20 in the Bayside profile; the Casey K 21.9 in the Casey profile; the rising main split as Pump.RisingMainSplitLps, Pump.RisingMainSmallMm, Pump.RisingMainLargeMm). Where a profile has no value the program says 'Casey K not set' and carries on (R-12, R-27), never a quiet code copy. Smallest fix: move the Bayside 1 in 20 and the Casey 21.9 into their profiles and read them from there; then add the reuse fields and the rising main boxes. Tim's word is needed on each council source and edition (engineering judgement). To SEE it: look for the reuse credit, the Bayside storm and the Casey K on the council page (today none is there); run CDDESIGN on a copy of a Kingston job with reuse tank volume and note the credit it takes off the storage, then try to change the credit from Settings (today it cannot be changed without a new build). ## BUG-539

**Command / Area:** R00_CIVIL item 1 (MEDIUM-HIGH, ENGINEERING-RESULT RISK; breaks R-00 'nothing hard-coded'; this is the Civil R-00 audit's number one; links to BUG-510, which found the CDCALC side): roofs and paving are always C 0.9 in CDDESIGN and in pump sizing, with no Settings name, while CDCALC's Boyd's tab counts them at 1.0. What the drafter sees: every design flow, detention volume and pump duty depends on this number, and nothing on the Settings page shows it. The soft-ground C (PostDevSoftGroundC) and the before-development C (PreDevWholeSiteC) do have Settings names (in the file only, no box); the hard-ground one does not. Evidence: Services/AutoDesignService.cs 55 (the constant) and 296 (CDDESIGN after-development flow); Services/PumpSizingService.cs 75 and 178-183 (pump sizing weighted C). The same value is also written separately in other screens: the CDCALC Boyd's tab counts roof and paved area at 1.0 (ViewModels/BoydsCalcViewModel.cs 182, from BUG-510); the Rational tab uses C 0.9 (ViewModels/RationalMethodViewModel.cs 353); the Charged system tab starts at 0.9 (ViewModels/ChargedSystemCalcViewModel.cs 10); the Detention Design tab starts at 0.85 (ViewModels/DetentionDesignViewModel.cs 19-25); the WSUD tab uses 0.85 (ViewModels/WsudViewModel.cs 22-24). The audit lists impervious C 0.9 / 0.85 (items 1, 22) as one of the seven places where screens disagree on one value. A wrong number on a design or on paper is the risk: two tools, or two tabs, give two storages for one site, and a drafter cannot tell which C the printed result used. Right result: one after-development hard-ground C, on the Settings page beside the soft-ground and before-development C (proposed DesignStandards.PostDevImperviousC, Runoff and rainfall tab, 'After-development runoff C for roofs and paving'), read by CDDESIGN, pump sizing, every CDCALC tab and the WSUD tab; the shipped value is for Tim to confirm. This is an office habit, not a standard. Smallest fix: add the one Settings row and read it in the two CDDESIGN places first (as BUG-510 says), then the tabs. To SEE it: open Settings, Civil, Runoff and rainfall and look for a roof-and-paving C (today none); on a copy of a job run CDDESIGN and CDCALC (Boyd's, Rational, Detention Design) on the same areas and compare the C each one uses (today 0.9, 1.0, 0.9 and 0.85). Change one council profile and the two screens give different holes, and nothing tells the drafter. ## BUG-550

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT routes 1, 2 and 3 (HIGH; BLOCKS COLLEAGUE INSTALL with gate item 10; same family and same fix as BUG-549, which named only CEMARKUP; this entry lists EVERY route in the markup / AI family so none is missed). Structural CEMARKUPBENCH, CEMARKUPPARSE, the CEMARKUP window's Parse button and CEMARKUP 'Ask AI' send job data to OpenAI, not Claude. (a) CEMARKUPBENCH uploads every PDF in a folder AND all its subfolders: Modules/Structural/Commands/MarkupAICommands.cs 304-383 (folder search is SearchOption.AllDirectories, line 347; default source mode Hybrid includes the upload, 339-344; default folder is the last markup folder or the Markups folder); upload in Services/MarkupAIVisionParser.cs 106-131 (POST files, purpose=user_data) then 133-179 (POST responses). Each whole PDF goes as bytes with its file name and a short prompt 'ProjectType=STR...'; nothing is blanked. OpenAI KEEPS every file because the code has no delete call (no HttpMethod.Delete anywhere in Structural). The command is listed, not hidden, in Assets/Config/command-registry.json 671. (b) CEMARKUPPARSE: MarkupAICommands.cs 53-88 then Services/MarkupAIWorkflowService.cs 39-62 then MarkupAIOrchestratorService.cs 64-66 then MarkupAIVisionParser.Parse. The whole PDF, its file name and the drawing type go to OpenAI when the drafter presses Enter at 'Source mode [Bluebeam/Hand/hYbrid] <Hybrid>'; only 'Bluebeam' avoids the upload; MarkupParseRequest.UseVisionParser also defaults to true (Models/MarkupAIModels.cs 64). The raw OpenAI reply is saved next to the package (MarkupAIWorkflowService.cs 78-83). (c) The CEMARKUP window's Parse button: UI/Palette/MarkupAIPanel.xaml.cs 143-146, the source combo defaults to Hybrid (MarkupAIPanel.xaml 48); same path as (b). (d) CEMARKUP 'Ask AI' chat: UI/Palette/MarkupAIPanel.xaml.cs 280-295 then Services/MarkupAIChatService.cs 32-83 (POST responses), payload built at 200-244. It sends the typed question, the package ID, the project code (worked out from the drawing name), the FULL DRAWING PATH (drawing = package.BaseDrawingPath, line 237; normally holds the Windows login and the client or job folder, for example C:\Users\<login>\OneDrive - ...\Projects\<job>), each markup item's text, layer and command, and up to 10 unresolved items with their raw text. The 'Enable chat' switch (MarkupAI.ChatEnabled) is honoured but DEFAULTS ON (MarkupAIModels.cs 238). THE SWITCH THAT DOES NOTHING: 'Enable MarkupAI' (MarkupAI.Enabled, default ON, MarkupAIModels.cs 224) is shown in CE Settings but is read by NOTHING before an upload, so a drafter who unticks it still uploads. The 'Share learning data' switch (MarkupAI.LearningDataOptIn, default ON) is also read by nothing; no data is shared by it but the label misleads. KEY AND ADDRESS: the key comes from the environment variable named in Settings (MarkupAI.OpenAiApiKeyEnvVar, default OPENAI_API_KEY, MarkupAIVisionParser.cs 45), never from a file; the web address is MarkupAI.OpenAiBaseUrl from the settings file (default https://api.openai.com/v1, MarkupAIModels.cs 227), so editing that file could send the key and the PDFs to any address. If no key is set, the commands skip and say 'Set environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY'. WHAT A DRAFTER SEES: nothing. No warning, no question, no tick-box: the PDF is simply uploaded when the drafter presses Enter at the Hybrid prompt, and the chat sends the job folder path on the button. On a job: a markup PDF carrying the client name and the site address sits on OpenAI's servers with no way for CE to remove it. TIM'S RULE, VERIFIED IN HIS OWN WORDS (UX-QA-05, 25/26 Sep): 'Yes, Claude only, page only (Recommended)': only the markup PAGE image goes, only to CLAUDE through CE's own connection (never OpenAI), never kept for training, with the title-block area blanked; and when the title block cannot be blanked, 'Don't send; say so (Recommended)': CE does not send that page and tells the user to tag that page's marks by hand. Sources: decisions\2026-09-25_V3_PLAN_DISCUSSION_RULINGS.md line 772 and 04_REFERENCE\structural\cards\STRUC-MARKUP-QA_CARD_2026-09-26.md lines 74-75 and 90. These routes break all three parts. TIM'S PC: no OPENAI_API_KEY is set in any scope (read by controller 06, see BUG-549), so nothing leaves today. A colleague PC with that variable set WOULD upload; the audit did not read any colleague PC. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fixes 1 and 2, for Tim to rule on): nothing leaves the PC unless a Settings value that DEFAULTS OFF is on. Make CEMARKUP read MarkupAI.Enabled before ANY upload and default it OFF (and ChatEnabled OFF) until the Claude route exists; or hide CEMARKUPPARSE, CEMARKUPBENCH and the Parse and Ask AI buttons for colleagues. When on: one page at a time, to Claude only, title block blanked or the page not sent; the chat never sends the drawing path; delete any provider-side copy; refuse a web address that is not the approved one. HOW TO SEE IT IN AUTOCAD: on a PC with a TEST key set, run CEMARKUPPARSE on a one-page PDF and press Enter at the Hybrid prompt: right = a plain message that markup AI is off and nothing sent (check the network or the provider's file list shows nothing new); CEMARKUPBENCH says off; the Parse button and Ask AI say off; Settings shows both switches OFF and unticking or ticking them changes the result. LINKS: BUG-549 (same family, same fix; this entry widens it), BUG-551 (Civil AI paths), gate item 10 in areas/release-v3-colleagues.md. ## BUG-551

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT routes 4 and 5 (HIGH; Civil AI paths that send consultant or markup pages to Claude; related to BUG-549 / BUG-550 and gate item 10). (a) CDIMPORTXCIVIL 'try AI extraction?' fallback: Modules/Drainage/Services/XcivilImportService.cs 763 then XcivilVisionFallbackOrchestrator.cs 61-153 then XcivilVisionScheduleExtractionService.cs 192-236; the command is Commands/LinkCommands.ImportXcivil.cs 29. It fires during CDIMPORTXCIVIL when CE's own schedule reading looks poor; the prompt is 'try AI extraction? [Yes/No] <Yes>' so ENTER = YES (XcivilVisionFallbackOrchestrator.cs 155-169). There is no switch in CE Settings; the only check is that a key is present (line 89). Unlike CDASK it has NO CE Cloud seat check, NO approved-provider policy check and NO 'Confidential project' check. A count of rows (no text) is added to the telemetry queue (146-150). (b) CDASK 'Analyse markups' and 'From file...': Controls/CeAssistantControl.xaml.cs 288-304 (screen) and 320-358 (file) then Services/MarkupAnalysisService.cs 68-166. It sends either a screenshot of the current AutoCAD view (title block included if it is on screen) or up to 5 PDF pages in ONE request (MarkupFileImageLoader.cs 47, MarkupAnalysisService.cs 160-163). Nothing is blanked. The gate here is good: a live CE Cloud seat with R2/W1 access, a project classified Standard (not Confidential), and an egress audit record that saves (xaml.cs 292-295, 324-327); the seat context only exists in CE Cloud mode (684-688). KEYS: environment variables only, read by Modules/Drainage/Services/CeAiEndpointResolver.cs 24-30. If CE_CLOUD_URL is set it uses the CE Cloud proxy with CE_CLOUD_AUTH; otherwise it goes DIRECT to api.anthropic.com with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (CE.AI.Core/IChatClient.cs 22, AnthropicChatClient.cs 120-125). CE_AI_APPROVED_PROVIDER_POLICY and the seat grant are read by CeAiSeatGrantService.cs 29-37. TIM'S RULE, VERIFIED IN HIS OWN WORDS (UX-QA-05, 25/26 Sep): 'Yes, Claude only, page only (Recommended)': only the markup PAGE image goes, only to CLAUDE through CE's own connection (never OpenAI), never kept for training, with the title-block area blanked; and when the title block cannot be blanked, 'Don't send; say so (Recommended)': CE does not send that page and tells the user to tag that page's marks by hand. Sources: decisions\2026-09-25_V3_PLAN_DISCUSSION_RULINGS.md line 772 and 04_REFERENCE\structural\cards\STRUC-MARKUP-QA_CARD_2026-09-26.md lines 74-75 and 90. Claude is the right provider for both paths, but several pages in one request and no title-block blanking break the rule, and (a) also skips the CE Cloud route the rest of Civil's AI uses. WHAT A DRAFTER SEES: in (a), a question in the middle of CDIMPORTXCIVIL; pressing Enter without reading it sends up to six pages of someone else's drawing set (consultant title blocks, job address) to an AI service. In (b), a button; the pages go after the gate passes, with no warning that the title block goes too. CE CLOUD PROXY (controller 06 read the worker source CE.Cloud/worker/src/worker.js at rel-20261009f, 809 lines): the proxy's handleMessagesPost forwards the request body UNCHANGED (await request.text()) to api.anthropic.com after checking the seat token. It does NOT limit pages, does NOT inspect images or PDFs and does NOT blank a title block. Its privacy line (never drawing content, file paths or project names) is enforced structurally on the TELEMETRY endpoint only. So Tim's 25 Sep rule is NOT applied server-side by the repo's worker; the DEPLOYED worker may differ and is not visible from the repo, so this is unproven either way. TIM'S PC (controller 06, read 9 Oct about 15:00, names and lengths only): CE_CLOUD_URL and CE_CLOUD_AUTH ARE SET (user scope, lengths 50 and 48) and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is NOT set, so on Tim's PC both Civil AI paths go through the CE Cloud proxy today. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fix 3, for Tim to rule on): gate the CDIMPORTXCIVIL fallback exactly like CDASK (CE Cloud seat, approved policy, non-Confidential project); default the prompt to No; send ONE page at a time with the title block blanked (or not sent). Give Analyse markups the same one-page-and-blank treatment. The blanking must happen on the PC before sending, because the proxy does not do it. HOW TO SEE IT IN AUTOCAD: run CDIMPORTXCIVIL on a consultant PDF CE reads poorly; right = the fallback question defaults to No, says plainly that pages leave the PC, and on Yes asks for one page at a time with the title block shown blanked in the preview; on a project marked Confidential it refuses. ## BUG-552

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT routes 9, 10 and 11 (MEDIUM-HIGH; the 'office folder, coded' rule is broken in THREE places). The rule, as the audit states it (not Tim's exact words): support zips and fault reports never leave the PC except into the office IT folder, and only coded (no real login, PC name or job names). (a) Civil fault reports reach the office IT folder UNCODED: Modules/Manager/Plugin.cs 137-152 (start-up plus 15 seconds) and Commands/PluginManagerCommands.cs 116 (CEMANAGERREFRESH) copy module telemetry through Services/CeAdminStorageService.cs 122-135 into <IT Admin>\CE Plugin Admin\. In Civil's records the drawing file name is in clear (Modules/Drainage/Services/AdminTelemetryService.cs 324 and 403) and the fault details are the raw error text (Details = ex.ToString(), line 176), which can hold full paths with the login and the client folder. Structural scrubs both (Modules/Structural/Services/AdminTelemetryService.cs 198-209, 428). SECOND PROBLEM in the same route: Civil and Structural write to %APPDATA%\TIM_CE_CADTOOLS\CE_Admin\outbox (Shared/CE_SHARED/Services/CeTelemetryStore.cs 60-68) but the Manager uploads from %APPDATA%\CE_CADTOOLS\CE_Admin\outbox and moves the old folder across only once, when the new one does not exist yet (CeAdminStorageService.cs 25-43). So Civil and Structural records probably reach the office folder only once, at that first move: a working-order problem as well as a privacy one (the audit did not check the real start-up order on a colleague PC). (b) CEMANAGERDIAG report has a coded file name but the REAL LOGIN INSIDE: Modules/Manager/Services/CeDiagnosticsService.cs 300-311 writes <IT Admin>\CE Diagnostics\<coded PC>\<time>_<coded login>.txt (or Desktop\CE Diagnostics when the IT folder is missing); the body carries the full IT Admin path, the OneDriveCommercial path and every loaded DLL path (96-101, 236), which normally include C:\Users\<login>. The body is not run through the scrubber. (c) Support zips are saved to the DESKTOP: Manager CESUPPORT, Services/CeSupportBundleService.cs 49-56 (Desktop\CE Diagnostics; contents scrubbed of login and PC name); Structural Services/SupportBundleService.cs 33-34 (Desktop\CE_Support_<time>.zip; logs and failures). CE uploads nothing itself, but company PCs often back the Desktop up to OneDrive, so the zip, with logs that name drawings and jobs, would sync into the person's own OneDrive and not the IT folder. The audit did not check any colleague's Desktop. WHAT A DRAFTER / COLLEAGUE SEES: nothing; they press 'Send a fault report' or run CESUPPORT / CEMANAGERDIAG and a file appears. On a job: the office IT folder (and, for the Desktop zips, possibly a personal OneDrive) holds files naming the real login and client job folders. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fixes 4 and 5, for Tim to rule on): run Civil's fault Message and Details through the same scrubber Structural uses; scrub the CEMANAGERDIAG report body (paths coded, no real login); save support zips to a local AppData folder first, then copy into the IT folder, coded; fix the two outbox folder names so they match. HOW TO SEE IT IN AUTOCAD: cause a Civil fault, run CEMANAGERREFRESH, open the new file in the IT folder: right = no real login, PC name, drawing name or client folder in it. Run CEMANAGERDIAG and search the report text for your Windows login: right = not found. Run CESUPPORT: right = the zip lands in an AppData folder or the IT folder, not the Desktop. LINKS (same family, some overlap, filed earlier from Audit 01): BUG-488 (CEMANAGERDIAG and the fault-report button write the real login, PC name and user folder: this audit's route 10 is the same fault), BUG-489 (CESUPPORT zip cleaner misses drawing names and paths), BUG-491 (A6 Manager failure reports, A7 Civil failure text not scrubbed and the same one-time move, A10 Structural's old support zip said to be dormant in 1.0.110). New here: the Desktop-syncs-to-OneDrive point and the Structural Desktop zip path in 1.0.112 (the audit names a 'diagnostics command'; BUG-491 A10 said no command reached it in 1.0.110, so whether it is reachable now is not established). AUDIT file: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\release-v3-colleagues-OFF_PC_CALLS_2026-10-09.md.

Structural writes real drawing names into the plugins' upload folder (usage records: Structural telemetry lines 364 and 428; machine report line 307), a HIGH when the #954 fault-record upload switch is ON (the default OFF touches nothing, so nothing leaks in any waiting payload today). #954 @ 0e51479e is MERGE-WITH-FIXES and stays out: upload ONLY Civil-marked records and delete the rest; the plugins' fault text goes through #941's path cutter (MEDIUM: fault records keep drawing and job-folder paths). ## BUG-553

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT route 13 (MEDIUM for security, LOW for job data): Structural CEMARKUPRUN installs software from the internet by default. Modules/Structural/Services/MarkupAIPyAutocadWorkerService.cs 335-355 runs python -m pip install pyautocad comtypes pywin32. No job data is sent; it downloads and installs code from PyPI (PyPI sees the PC's address and Python version) into the colleague's own Python. It happens the first time a CEMARKUP batch uses the Python worker and those packages are missing. The switch MarkupAI.AutoBootstrapPyAutocadWorker DEFAULTS ON (Models/MarkupAIModels.cs 236). Tim's rules do not cover this; it is an unvetted internet download. WHAT A DRAFTER SEES: a markup batch pauses while software installs, with no question first; on a locked-down office PC it may fail, on another it installs unvetted code. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fix 7, for Tim to rule on): default AutoBootstrapPyAutocadWorker to OFF; when the packages are missing, say so and name what to install, rather than installing. Better still, ship the needed packages with the plugin or the IT-approved Python. HOW TO SEE IT: on a PC without those packages, run a CEMARKUP batch: right = a clear message that the helper is missing and nothing is downloaded (no pip window, no network call). ## BUG-558

**Command / Area:** Undo / Redo across a drawing switch, Civil. Found by the Claude driver tester (run 2, 9 Oct 22:25-22:47, test copy C:\ce_rc_drv\CLD10_B1.dwg, Civil 3.0.41 / Manager 1.1.41, AutoCAD 2027). Report: areas/release-v3-colleagues-CLAUDE_DRIVER_RUN2_2026-10-09.md check 3. MEDIUM until the cause is known.

**What happens:** on the Civil copy, U, switch to another open drawing, switch back, REDO says 'Nothing to redo'. 3 times out of 3 (a pit MOVE; a plain CIRCLE; the same circle with only 4 s between steps). The same chain on the Structural copy (CLD10_S1, CE Structural 1.0.110) worked 1 of 1 ('Everything has been redone'). The no-switch control on the Civil copy passes (U, 15 s, REDO). Autosave also breaks REDO but that is AutoCAD's own rule, proved with a plain CIRCLE, and is not this bug.

**Cause NOT proven:** may be CE Civil writing to the drawing at document activation, or AutoCAD itself (the Civil copy has four missing background xrefs, 'Background not found: XW2626-Title Block ... XW2614-Arch Site'), or something particular to that copy. To prove: repeat on a Civil copy with NO missing xrefs (for example DRV15_METRE.dwg), look in the CE log for a write at activation, and use the test-only witness recorder (queued for build/03) to list every command, lock and object change between the U and the REDO. Added to Codex brief W49 as item W49-07b. Redo-safety link: RedoSafeCallGraphTests has blind spots per BUG-457.

**UPDATE 10 Oct 02:20, Codex W49 (report CODEX_VERIFYW49_2026-10-10.md items 16, 26, 31, 39): REPRODUCED TWICE by Codex, so the driver's run 3 pass does not close it. W49-02 Civil: PIT placed, U (echo PIT), switched to the other drawing by tab clicks (57 s and 66 s after the U), back, REDO after 77 s = 'Nothing to redo', SAVETIME 0 so no autosave. W49-07b Structural: plain CIRCLE 0,0 50, U, switch to Civil and back (32 s and 79 s after the U), REDO after 96 s = 'Nothing to redo'. **Command / Area:** PIT and Edit Pit with the layer of the pit's text locked, Civil 3.0.44 (Codex W58-02 and W58-03, 10 Oct 10:05 to 10:20, report CODEX_VERIFYW58_2026-10-10.md; the protections of PRs #880 to #885 and the HUNT-C-03 pre-check are installed). MEDIUM to HIGH until explained.

**What happens:** on DWG-B1_VC7 the typed lookup (ssget on the text 'P2', 33 hits, item 0) returned the label layer 35TEXT; the pit block P2 is on STORMWATER PIT. With 35TEXT LOCKED: (1) Edit Pit (X size 900 to 1050, Save) printed '[CE] Error during PITEDIT - see CE log for details.' instead of the plain refusal sentence, the pit and its Pit Schedule row stayed 900 x 900, and U twice echoed PITSCHEDULE then PITEDIT (an undo step was left); (2) PIT placed a new pit P97 and printed '[CE] Pit retained without its number label: the label could not be written safely.' (no refusal BEFORE placing; the cover text CL 18.000 was placed). Both are the OLD faults the protections were meant to remove. #870 (PIT during REFEDIT) WORKS: '[CE] PIT cannot run while a reference is being edited in place (REFEDIT). Finish or close it (REFCLOSE) first. Nothing was changed.'

**Code reading (controller, read only, rel-20261009o):** PitCommand.cs:312-319 calls PitAnnotationLockRule.RefusalForNewPit, which tests only the FIXED layer names LayerService.LAYER_PIT_LABEL = 'STORMWATER PIT LABEL' and LAYER_PIPE_TEXT = '25TEXT' (Rules/PitAnnotationLockRule.cs). If this drawing writes the pit number label on 35TEXT (a layer chosen by Settings / text size / the drawing's own layer map), the pre-check never sees the lock and the write fails afterwards, exactly as seen. Edit Pit's check (PitEditCommand.cs:644-661) reads the layer of the pit's actual annotation objects, so it should have caught a label really on 35TEXT: therefore it is also possible that the text found by the typed lookup (item 0 of 33 'P2' texts) was NOT the pit's own label (35TEXT is also the Pit Schedule and long-section text layer: PitScheduleViewModel.cs:184, LongitudinalSectionService.cs:292), and the error then comes from the Pit Schedule update writing its table on the locked 35TEXT. Either way the result is a CE error line instead of a plain refusal, so the protection has a gap.

**Next step (Civil lane, RED test first):** (a) find which layer the new pit's number label and the Pit Schedule table text are really written on in this drawing and make the pre-check use the SAME resolver (R-00: no fixed name); (b) add every layer the command or its linked schedule update will write to into the pre-check of PIT, Edit Pit and the schedule update; (c) rerun with the lock on the label layer read from the pit's OWN label (handle), not from a text search. Also noted: the first U after the failed Edit Pit echoed PITSCHEDULE (the schedule update left its own undo step).

**ROOT CAUSE (Claude tester run 15, 10 Oct 10:55, AutoCAD closed, no Codex active; supersedes the two guesses above):** the pit NUMBER is an ATTRIBUTE inside the label block and the attribute DEFINITION is on layer 35TEXT (all 11 labels agree); the label block itself is on STORMWATER PIT LABEL; the cover text MTEXT is on 25TEXT; the pit is on STORMWATER PIT. PitAnnotationLockRule checks only the middle two (label block layer and cover text layer), so with 35TEXT locked there is no up-front refusal, and the write of the attribute then fails. The Pit Schedule theory is NOT needed. ## BUG-566

**Command / Area:** Structural menu load at start-up (Modules/Structural/Services/CuiMenuGeneratorService.cs about line 1421), found by the Opus review round 10 while reviewing PR #1231 (Manager leaveMenuBarAlone), Mon 12 Oct 2026. MEDIUM.

**What happens (code reading, not seen in AutoCAD):** after every update Structural's own menu load sets the MENUBAR system variable to 1 without checking what it was, at start-up on an automatic path. ## BUG-697

**Command / Area:** CD, first question, option E ("Existing line"), Civil 3.0.53 (found by Claude driver run 25, 18 Oct 2026, real AutoCAD 2027 on a test copy).

**Symptom:** Type CD, answer E, then pick a plain polyline you drew yourself. CE says "[CE] That line is already a CE pipe. Double-click it to change it. Nothing was changed." and then "[CE] CD command cancelled." It does this for every plain polyline: tried a closed rectangle twice and an open 3-point line, all on layer BLOCKS, none of them a CE pipe. The pipe window never opens, so "use a drawn line as the pipe" cannot be used at all. This also stops the closed-line fix (BUG-684) from being tested.

**Expected behaviour:** A plain drawn polyline is accepted as the pipe route ("[CE] Using the drawn line (N points) as the pipe route."), and only a line that already is a CE pipe gets the "already a CE pipe" message.

**Reference:** Source read at b06126db: `Modules/Drainage/Commands/CdCommand.ExistingLine.cs` line 125 treats `PipePickService.TryResolvePipe(...)` returning true as "already a pipe", but `Services/PipePickService.cs` `TryResolvePipe` returns true for ANY polyline (its test is "is a Polyline"). That test has been in CD since the Existing-line feature (commit f93d44db, 5 Sep). I have not run an older build, so I do not know if this ever worked. Report: `areas/release-v3-colleagues-CLAUDE_DRIVER_RUN25_CIVIL3053_2026-10-18.md`, check 1.

**Status:** FIXED (Claude-accepted, Civil 3.0.75, 25 Oct 2026): runner case R39 (CD then E on a plain line opens the new-pipe window, no false "already a CE pipe") passed in two separate sessions on 3.0.75, its broken variant fails, and the independent review (areas\RUNNER_CASE_REVIEW_B3FIX_2026-10-25.md) agrees. The other half (picking an existing CE pipe still says "already a CE pipe") is a separate check. Not Tim-confirmed in his own drawings.

## BUG-856

**Command / Area:** CDTIDYLABELS (Tidy labels) — the "Will move ..." window line.

**Symptom:** When Tidy labels offers to move a label, the line says only "a pipe's start invert text would move 235 mm (the other side)". It does not say WHICH pipe the text belongs to. On a drawing with many pipes the drafter cannot tell which label is about to move before answering Yes. Seen on run 37 (3.0.61) with an ordinary block moved onto the P8 start text: the "No clear spot" line named P4 -> P3 but the "would move" line named no pipe.

**Expected behaviour:** The "would move" line names the pipe, the same way the "No clear spot found" line does (for example "pipe P8 -> Open end start invert text would move 235 mm (the other side)").

**Reference:** Civil Tidy labels report wording; evidence CLAUDE_DRIVER_RUN37_V2_2026-10-20.md B item 5. LOW (wording only, no drawing change). Test that would catch it: a fixture with one text moved onto an ordinary block, run Tidy labels, assert the "would move" line contains the pipe name. **Symptom:** importing `150x90x10 L ]L LINTEL` prints `150 x 90 x 10 EA LINTEL`. Expected `150 x 90 x 10 UA LINTEL`; equal angles remain EA. The old exception recognises only `150x100x10` and can classify several angles in one cell from that one size.

**Status:** OPEN — built and unit-tested in the same draft PR #1533 and report as above. All 57 catalogue angle sizes (38 EA, 19 UA), worked examples and mixed-angle cells pass; 18 catalogue unequal-angle glyph cases failed before. Plain UA input already kept UA: the defect specifically needs the Excel `L ]L` glyph. No Settings switch: incorrect section labels are defects. Not installed or AutoCAD-accepted; the real placed-schedule check remains pending.

## BUG-1035 — Pit Schedule decides "Shallow" from a hidden fixed 300 mm depth

**Command / Area:** PITSCHEDULE, STATE column and caution colour, Civil 3.0.72 (Codex audit RD01-01, 23 Oct 2026). MEDIUM, SURE (verified by reading; not run in AutoCAD).

**Symptom:** A pit 290 mm deep reads "Shallow" and a pit 310 mm deep reads "OK". The 300 mm line is fixed in the program and there is no shallow-pit depth box on the Settings page, so an office that wants to review pits shallower than, say, 450 mm cannot say so. A 310 mm pit gets "OK" and no caution colour.

**Expected behaviour:** The shallow-pit depth is a named value with a plain-English box on the Settings page (CDS > Pipes and Pits). Keep 300 mm as the starting value until Tim says otherwise. The result stays a warning only (R-27). Do not borrow the minimum pipe cover: pit depth and cover over a pipe are different measurements.

**Reference:** CODEX_AUDIT2_RD01_23OCT.md finding RD01-01; `Modules/Drainage/ViewModels/PitScheduleViewModel.cs:38` (private constant `ShallowDepthThreshold = 0.30`), `PitScheduleViewModel.Data.cs:2183,2196`, `PitScheduleRow.cs:505`, `Dialogs/PitScheduleDialog.xaml:620,628`. Impact: an engineering threshold the office cannot see or change (R-00 Settings-first). Existing: none (grepped Shallow, ShallowDepthThreshold). Fix kind: settings row plus one reader. Protected: no. Lane: Sonnet; base claude/rel-20261023m.

**Test that catches it:** drive `AddRowCommand` and the real Depth-change handler (not a copied comparison): manual rows with Depth 0.29, 0.30 and 0.31 give STATE "Shallow", "OK", "OK" today; after the fix, with the new Settings value set to 450 mm, all three say "Shallow". A second test asserts the Settings page defines the new row.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** new millimetre drawing with no linked pits. Type PITSCHEDULE, untick "Auto-calculate depth", click "+ Add Row" three times (AUDIT-A, B, C), leave levels empty, type Depth 0.29, 0.30, 0.31 (Tab after each). Right looks like: after the fix and with the Settings value at 450, all three rows read "Shallow". Then type CDS and check Pipes and Pits has the shallow-pit depth box. Restore the Settings file byte for byte afterwards.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1040 — Keeping a hand-typed pipe level can refuse the whole cascade

**Command / Area:** CDPROPAGATE and the Edit Pipe downstream cascade (Keep answer), Civil 3.0.72 (Codex audit RD03-01, 23 Oct 2026). HIGH, SURE (verified by reading).

**Symptom:** Keep P1 at RL 10.20 (typed by hand), raise downstream P2 to RL 10.30, answer Keep. If keeping makes that pipe flat or uphill, CE refuses every proposed change: "[CDPROPAGATE] Apply blocked - keeping the level typed by hand on P1 -> P2 would leave the pipe flat or running backwards. Nothing was changed. Check that pipe's level, or run CDPROPAGATE and choose Overwrite ..." The preview also greys Apply ("1 pipe(s) would have flat/negative grade - Apply blocked"). ## BUG-1064 — Two installers running at once can put the old Civil back after a successful install

**Command / Area:** the CE installer `--activate-staged` route, Civil/Manager 3.0.72 / 1.1.72 (Codex audit RD08-01, 23 Oct 2026). HIGH, SURE under the stated conditions (verified by reading; not seen in the office).

**Symptom:** An operator retries an update while the first copy is still finishing. The retry reports "The signed verified bundle was installed." The first copy then fails at its last record save and puts the old Civil back over the new one. After reopening AutoCAD the drafter has the older Civil, and a Manager updated in between can leave the pair from different releases.

**Expected behaviour:** One machine-wide installation lock from the final checks to the end of recovery; a second run waits with a plain message and re-checks the target once it owns the lock. No new permanent block (R-27).

**Reference:** CODEX_AUDIT2_RD08_23OCT.md finding RD08-01; `Installer/SafeBundleInstaller.cs:293,308,334,340,347,358,361`, entry `Installer/CeInstallerApplication.cs:134`. Ordinary Manager use does not trigger it (nothing calls `CeFinishUpdatePlanner` in production). Impact: a successful install silently undone. Existing: none (grepped installation lock, overlapping activations; BUG-823/886 are other installer faults). Fix kind: code. Protected: yes (installer). Lane: Opus.

**Test that catches it:** use the existing `SafeBundleInstallerTests` signed fixture in disposable folders: run installer A, and inside its `beforeCommit` callback run installer B (returns Installed) then throw an IOException. After a fix B must wait, or A must not restore over B's live target.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** not an AutoCAD test (AutoCAD must be closed): run the fixture test above on a disposable copy and read the installer messages and the final bundle hash. Never run against the live plugin folders.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1065 — A failed first install can leave the suite's loading file behind with no warning

**Command / Area:** the CE installer, adding a missing bundle, Civil/Manager 3.0.72 / 1.1.72 (Codex audit RD08-02, 23 Oct 2026). MEDIUM, SURE under the stated conditions (verified by reading).

**Symptom:** CE is adding a suite that was not installed. The last record save fails while another process holds a new file open. The installer says "Installation failed before a safe cutover completed" but its clean-up error is swallowed, so the live `PackageContents.xml` can stay. The next AutoCAD start may load the rejected install or half of it.

**Expected behaviour:** The rejected live bundle is retired, the result is checked, and if either step fails the installer says plainly that recovery is needed and names the surviving path. Failed clean-up of the live folder is never treated as harmless.

**Reference:** CODEX_AUDIT2_RD08_23OCT.md finding RD08-02; `Installer/SafeBundleInstaller.cs:363,365,383,661,674,677` (`DeleteGeneratedDirectory` suppresses every error), `Installer/CeInstallerApplication.cs:140,141`. Impact: a half-installed suite on the next start. Existing: none (grepped DeleteGeneratedDirectory). Fix kind: code. Protected: yes. Lane: Opus.

**Test that catches it:** fixture with no existing target; in `beforeCommit` hold the promoted `PackageContents.xml` open with no delete sharing, then throw. A failed result must leave no active manifest, or must say recovery is needed.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** not an AutoCAD test: run the fixture test on disposable folders, read the installer message and look for `PackageContents.xml` at the target.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1080 — CDREFRESHBLOCKS changes the shared symbol that locked copies use

**Command / Area:** CDREFRESHBLOCKS (RISER, DROPPER, PIT LABEL, PIT LABEL 2), Civil 3.0.72 (Codex audit RD12-01, 23 Oct 2026). HIGH (native protection), SURE (verified by reading).

**Symptom:** A riser or pit-label symbol on a locked layer, locked to protect finished work, changes shape after CDREFRESHBLOCKS. The command only checks the block name and the source file, then replaces the shared definition (`db.Insert(blockName, sourceDb, true)`), so every copy changes whatever its layer lock says. The layer stays locked, so the flag gives false reassurance. There is also no REFEDIT check at the start.

**Expected behaviour:** Before replacing a definition, check every copy, including copies inside other blocks. If any is protected or cannot be proved safe, leave that definition alone and say which symbol and layer was skipped. Never unlock, clone around or swap the protected copy.

**Reference:** CODEX_AUDIT2_RD12_23OCT.md finding RD12-01; `Modules/Drainage/Commands/RefreshBlocksCommand.cs:54,67,114,121`, `Services/BlockService.cs:684-689`, `Commands/CeCommandBase.cs:19-24`. Impact: a locked detail changes without warning (native protection rule). Existing: none (grepped CDREFRESHBLOCKS; the older entries describe adding the command and the pit migration). Fix kind: code. Protected: yes. Lane: Opus.

**Test that catches it:** resident RISER definition with an extra circle (radius 123 at 7000,7000), a copy on locked layer AUDIT-LOCK: after CDREFRESHBLOCKS the circle must still be there and a skip message must name the symbol and layer (today it disappears and the log says "redefined 'RISER'"). Repeat with the copy nested inside a locked parent insert.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** synthetic drawing with a resident RISER (extra circle as above), a RISER copy on locked layer AUDIT-LOCK, current layer 0. Type CDREFRESHBLOCKS then REGEN. Right looks like: the extra circle is still drawn and CE names the skipped protected symbol.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1088 — The automatic pipe sizer picks the smallest pipe at any grade, up to 1 in 1

**Command / Area:** CDDESIGN connection pipe, network redesign, CDRUNSOLVE and auto-design (pipe sizing), Civil 3.0.72 (Opus Team audit T1 finding 1, 24 Oct 2026). HIGH, SURE (read end to end and worked by hand).

**Symptom:** The sizer tries pipe sizes smallest first and returns the first one that works at ANY grade, as steep as 1 in 1, limited only by a 6 m/s speed cap. For UPVC: 40 L/s comes out DN100 at about 1 in 2.8 (5.1 m/s) where DN225 at 1 in 200 carries 41.3 L/s; 25 L/s comes out DN100 at 1 in 7; 100 L/s comes out DN150 at 1 in 3.9 where DN375 at 1 in 300 carries 132 L/s. On a job: a 30 m network-redesign pipe at 1 in 3.9 falls 7.7 m, the pits below are metres deep and a council connection cannot be reached, yet the preview offers it as a feasible design. It does not show in CDRUNSOLVE today only because that command feeds no flow (BUG-999); once flows are fed it will.

**Expected behaviour:** The sizer takes the smallest size that works at or flatter than a preferred design grade, and goes steeper only when no size on the ladder works. The preferred grade is a Settings value (needs Tim's ruling on the number).

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T1_24OCT.md finding 1; `Modules/Drainage/Services/PipeSizingSolver.cs:131,136,168-186`, `Services/SettingsSizingStandards.cs:67-74`, `AutoDesignService.cs:656-680`, `NetworkDesignService.cs:290`. Existing: none (grepped sizer steepest grade; BUG-868 is the UPVC-only assumption, BUG-999 the missing flow). Fix kind: code plus a Settings value. Protected: no. Lane: Opus after Tim's ruling.

**Test that catches it:** unit case: size 40 L/s UPVC and assert the proposed grade is not steeper than the preferred design grade when a larger size at a flatter grade also works.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** CDDESIGN on a test copy with a 40 L/s connection pipe. Right looks like: a DN225 or larger pipe at a sensible grade (about 1 in 200), not DN100 at 1 in 3.

**Status:** OPEN

So the two answer opposite ways on the same pipe: a DN300 concrete pipe at 1 in 600 runs at 0.56 m/s, CDCALC shows no warning but CDRULES warns "below 0.6 m/s"; a DN375 concrete pipe at 1 in 20 runs at 3.55 m/s, CDCALC says "check for scour risk" but CDRULES passes it.

**Expected behaviour:** Pipe Flows uses the Settings minimum and the material's speed cap (the general maximum when no material is known), the same as CDRULES.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T1_24OCT.md finding 2; `Modules/Drainage/ViewModels/PipeFlowCalcViewModel.cs:268-271`. Existing: none (BUG-1036 is the roughness note on the same tab; BUG-544 is other ignored Settings). Fix kind: code. Protected: no.

**Test that catches it:** unit case: DN300 concrete at 1 in 600 must warn minimum speed; DN375 concrete at 1 in 20 must not warn scour.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** CDCALC, Pipe Flows, enter DN300 concrete at 1 in 600, then run CDRULES on a matching pipe. Right looks like: both warn "below 0.6 m/s".

**Status:** OPEN

**Symptom:** 17 council profiles carry the text "(0.3*pervious + 0.9*impervious)/site" while holding perviousC 0.35. CDRULES or the source viewer shows 0.35 with that working beside it; a checker reproducing it gets 0.30. CR-A1 point 3 says the printed working must show the number actually used. First written up 15 Sep (FINDING_PERVIOUS_C_SPLIT), answered by CR-A1, text never corrected. CDDESIGN's own C is right.

**Expected behaviour:** Rebuild the text from the numbers actually used, or drop the formula string.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T2_24OCT.md finding 17; `council-profiles.json` preDevCFormula, `Rules/CouncilRuleValues.cs:127-135`, `Models/CouncilProfileModels.cs:113`. Existing: none. Fix kind: data.

**Test that catches it:** case: every profile's printed working reproduces its printed number.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** CDRULEBOOK on a Whitehorse test copy, open the before-development C source. Right looks like: the working shows 0.35.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1112 — WSUD export prints a sample site nobody typed

**Command / Area:** CDCALC WSUD tab export, Civil 3.0.72 (T2 finding 18). LOW, SURE.

**Symptom:** The tab is read-only but its "WSUD / annual load reduction" export box still works and writes "Total site area 1000 m2, Impervious 200 / 700 m2, 630 mm rain" into the computations package as if they were the job's figures (R-12). The drafter cannot correct them.

**Expected behaviour:** Blank starting values, or untick and disable the export while the tab is read-only.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T2_24OCT.md finding 18; `ViewModels/WsudViewModel.cs:19-24`, `Dialogs/CalculationsV2Dialog.xaml:1309`, `Services/CalculationExportPackage.cs:503-530`. Existing: none (BUG-547 is the fixed targets). Fix kind: code.

**Test that catches it:** case: the export with default inputs writes no sample figures.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** CDCALC, tick the WSUD export, prepare the package. Right looks like: no 1000 m2 site in the package.

**Status:** OPEN

**Evidence note (CE 05, 30 Oct 2026, from draft PR #1877 = B-061 and Opus pre-review N, areas\OPUS_PREREVIEW_N_1877_BUG1112_30OCT.md):** verdict KEEP-WITH-NOTE for the next Civil train on claude/rel-20261102a. With the switch (linking.wsudExportSkipsSampleSite, ON; settings file only, a Settings-page row to be added after #1875) the site area, both impervious areas and all four runoff lines read "not entered". Limits found: (1) the author's report was wrong that a drafter can "type 850": every box on the CDCALC WSUD tab is read-only, so the robot case C32_wsud_export_sample as first written cannot run (the reviewer wrote a replacement case in the review); (2) "not entered" is decided by whether any of the three boxes changed since the window opened, not by the number: a saved calculation holding exactly 1000 / 200 / 700 would read "not entered" (low risk), and once one box changes all three print (a real site area beside the untouched 200 / 700 would print 200 / 700 as the job's); (3) the 630 mm rainfall and the two C figures still print (they come from Settings); this reading belongs to BUG-1112; (4) the failed test (PDF to picture) is an old fault on the Edge browser engine, not AutoCAD's renderer. Not proven in AutoCAD. Still OPEN.

**Expected behaviour:** A prefix only counts when the next character of the section name is a letter, never a digit or decimal point. `310UB3` still finds 310UB32; `114.3x6` says "no section called 114.3x6".

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T3_24OCT.md finding 1; `Modules/Structural.DesignCore/SteelSections/CeMemberPrompts.cs:101-117`, `Commands/CeMemberCommands.cs:372`. Existing: none (grepped CEMEMBER 114.3; BUG-818 is wrong list figures). Fix kind: code.

**Status:** OPEN

**Evidence note (CE 05, 31 Oct 2026, from job s5 report areas\BUGFIX_s5_REPORT_31OCT.md; built and unit-tested only):** draft PR #1900 (head 7fd49669, base claude/rel-20261026s; title has no B number yet, CE 01 gives B-081): at the CEMEMBER "Section name" prompt, typing 114.3x6, 168.3x6, 60.3x4 or 89x89x3 used to pick the 6.4, 6.4, 4.5 or 3.5 wall without saying so; now CEMEMBER says there is no section called that. 114.3x6.4 and 114.3x6.4chs still work; 310UB3 still finds 310UB32. Switch CeMember.SectionNamePrefixStopsAtDecimalPoint, ON (settings file only; off = old behaviour). Files: CeMemberPrompts.cs, CeMemberCommands.cs, UserSettings.cs. Needs an AutoCAD look. Still OPEN.
