## BUG-1135 — An older CE silently deletes newer parts of the job record, and the "newer CE" warning can never fire

**Command / Area:** Civil job record (ProjectData) save, Civil 3.0.72 and earlier builds (Opus Team audit T4-01, 24 Oct 2026). HIGH, SURE.

**Symptom:** The job record has no catch-all for unknown fields (pits and pipes do). The version marker has read "2.2" since 25 Aug, while fields added since (held-back plan labels 2 Oct, IgnoredChecks 9 Oct, PausedFeatures 9 Oct, Project Review approvals 27 Sep) never raised it. The save writes the whole record from the building build's own field list, and normalising stamps the version back to "2.2", so even a later bump shows once and is erased. On a job: Tim ignores three CDCHECKS cover findings and approves the review on 3.0.72; a colleague on an older 3.0.6x build changes one pit's lid type and saves; back on Tim's PC the findings are back, the approval is gone and held-back labels are forgotten. Nobody is told.

**Expected behaviour:** Catch-all for unknown fields on the job record and its nested lists; bump the marker whenever a field is added; never write a lower version over a higher one; hold the save as BUG-971 intends.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T4_24OCT.md T4-01; `Models/ProjectData.cs:10`, `Services/ProjectDataStorageContract.cs:12`, `ProjectDataService.Persistence.cs:597-609,1121-1124`, `ProjectDataService.Mutations.cs:1967`. Existing: none (BUG-971 is a record that cannot be read; here it reads and still loses data). Fix kind: code. Protected: no. Lane: Opus.

**Test that catches it:** round-trip case: a record with IgnoredChecks written by the new build, loaded and saved by a build that does not know the field, still holds it.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** on a test copy ignore a CDCHECKS finding on 3.0.72, save, open and save from the older 3.0.6x build, reopen on 3.0.72. Right looks like: the ignored finding is still ignored.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1165 — An old Civil bundle in the all-users folder supplies the pit blocks first

**Command / Area:** PIT and fall-symbol block lookup on a hand-installed PC (9 Nov colleague install), Civil 3.0.72 (Opus Team audit T5 finding 1, 24 Oct 2026). MEDIUM, SURE.

**Symptom:** The block search order is ProgramData first, then Program Files, then the user's own %APPDATA% copy. If Max once had Civil installed for all users by the old office installer, the hand copy cannot remove that copy without an administrator, and PIT drops the old office pit block and old fall symbols, not the 3.0.72 blocks. No warning; the pit just looks like last year's. The fallback `assemblyDir\Blocks` points at a folder that never exists, so a bundle copied anywhere else finds no blocks at all.

**Expected behaviour:** Search the running bundle's own `Contents\Blocks` first (RuntimePathService.GetBundleRoot()). Until then an administrator checks and clears `C:\ProgramData\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins` and `C:\Program Files\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins` before 9 Nov.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T5_24OCT.md finding 1; `Modules/Drainage/Services/BlockService.cs:101-109`. Existing: BUG-483 (stale ProgramData copies) is known; the block order is new. Fix kind: code. Protected: no.

**Test that catches it:** case: a stale bundle in a fake ProgramData folder and a newer bundle in %APPDATA%; the newer block is the one inserted.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** test PC with a marked old block in a fake all-users bundle and the new blocks in %APPDATA%; type PIT. Right looks like: the 3.0.72 pit block, not the old one.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1173 — The colleague pack's backup step saves only 2 of the CE settings folders

**Command / Area:** colleague pack page 02 step 4 and rollback, Manager 1.1.72 (T5 finding 9). LOW, SURE.

**Symptom:** The step copies `%APPDATA%\TIM_CE_CADTOOLS` and `%APPDATA%\CE_CVL_SUITE`. 1.1.72 also writes `%APPDATA%\CE_CADTOOLS` (Manager storage and menu), `%APPDATA%\Creative Engineering\CE Suite Manager` (CE Blocks) and `%APPDATA%\CE_SUITE_MANAGER\logs`. These stay behind on rollback, and the CE Manager pull-down menu may stay loaded with no commands behind it (UNSURE).

**Expected behaviour:** Add the three folders to step 4, and add "MENULOAD, unload CE_SUITE_MANAGER_MENU" to the rollback.

**Reference:** TEAM_AUDIT_T5_24OCT.md finding 9; `Modules/Manager/Services/CeAdminStorageService.cs:33`, `CeSuiteManagerMenuService.cs:137`, `CeBlocksSettings.cs:35`, `CommandOutcomeInfoLog.cs:12`. Existing: none. Fix kind: document.

**Test that catches it:** rehearsal: after rollback no CE_CADTOOLS or CE Suite Manager folder remains and the menu is gone.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** rollback rehearsal on a spare login; open AutoCAD. Right looks like: no CE Manager menu and no leftover folders.

**Status:** OPEN

**Evidence note (CE 05, 30 Oct 2026, from job p1 report areas\BUGFIX_p1_REPORT_30OCT.md and CE 00 Opus pre-review L):** no code fault; the backup is a manual step in the colleague pack (page 02 lists five folders: %APPDATA%\TIM_CE_CADTOOLS, CE_CVL_SUITE, CE_CADTOOLS, Creative Engineering\CE Suite Manager, CE_SUITE_MANAGER\logs, all confirmed written by code). Pack line to add: "also %APPDATA%\CE_SUITE if it exists" (an optional hand-written Manager switch file, CeOneGlanceStatus.cs line 314; it does not exist on Tim's PC today), and "if a _PRE_V3 folder already exists, stop and tell the desk, never copy over it". SECURITY: on an administrator's PC that folder may still hold an old blob-config.local.json with a write key (SEC-001 history): a local backup copy is fine but it must NEVER be zipped, emailed or sent; question for CE 01: add it to the CESUPPORT support-zip exclusion check. Pack wording not yet edited. Still OPEN until Tim confirms.

**Evidence note 2 (CE 05, 30 Oct 2026, facts from CE 01, code on claude/rel-20261102a; no file contents read):** no path under %APPDATA%\CE_SUITE can reach the CESUPPORT support zip. The zip collects only the CE_CADTOOLS\CE_Admin logs and sessions folders, the Desktop "CE Diagnostics" folder, the latest office diagnostics text and the plug-in log folders (top level, CE's own log names, last 14 days). Nothing in the code reads blob-config.local.json any more (the Azure upload code was deleted) and the zip is made on the PC only, never uploaded. Only gap, by file NAME: the CE_Admin\logs, CE_Admin\sessions and "CE Diagnostics" folders are walked into every sub-folder and accept any .json, so a key or settings file copied into one of them would be zipped. Defence-in-depth fix: B-063 (register item 84), a Max agent building a Manager-only draft that skips blob-config*, *.local.json and anything under a CE_SUITE folder; no Settings switch (it only narrows what is zipped). The question for CE 01 in the note above is therefore answered.

## BUG-1229 — New Pipe, "Set my own" with "I know one end": the grade box and the worked-out downstream level end up shallower (1 in 102) than the grade the drafter wanted

**Command / Area:** CD (New Pipe window), pipe grade "Set my own" + "I know one end - work the other out from the grade", Civil 3.0.85 (Tim's PC, by hand, 29 Oct 2026). WRONG ANSWER, severity to confirm.

**Symptom:** P10 to P9, 100 mm UPVC. Upstream level typed 19.45, the window worked the downstream out as 19.36 (a 90 mm fall) and the grade box reads "1 in 102". Tim: "it rounding to 1 in 102 which is shallower than what it should be". Not yet known: the pipe length, and whether Tim typed 100 and the window changed it to 102, or typed 102. By my reading of the code (not seen in AutoCAD): the fall is length divided by the grade, always rounded UP to the next 10 mm, which should make a pipe steeper than the chosen grade, never shallower; 1 in 102 with a 90 mm fall suggests the grade box is being overwritten from a rounded result, or the length used is not the drawn length. This is a guess to be checked, not a finding.

**Expected behaviour:** A grade the drafter picks (for example 1 in 100) is a minimum: the calculated level gives that grade or steeper, never shallower, and the grade box keeps what he typed. Tim's words: "it rounding to 1 in 102 which is shallower than what it should be".

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) Run CD from P10 to P9, choose Set my own 1 in 100 and "I know one end", type 19.45 upstream. (2) Read the downstream level and the grade box. (3) Compare 90 mm fall against the drawn pipe length divided by 100. Right = fall is at least length divided by 100 and the box still says 100.

**Reference:** Tim's screenshot 1 (29 Oct 2026, desk chat). Code read at commit 09126560: CdCommand.Grade.cs, MathHelper.CalculateInvertDrop and ApplyCalculatedInvertRule. Related: BUG-199, BUG-866..872 (Opus audit 22 Oct: "grade on straight distance"), AUDIT_ENGINEERING_CIVIL_2026-10-22.md (round-up ignores the decimals setting).

**Tim answered 29 Oct (later):** "i just typed the first invert. 9.2m". So the pipe is 9.2 m long and only the upstream level was typed; the grade box was NOT typed by Tim. **Cause found by arithmetic and code reading (commit 09126560, not yet seen live):** typing the first level runs the "suggest downstream" step (UpstreamDownstreamSuggest.SuggestFromStandardGrade): fall = 9.2 / 100 = 0.092 m, downstream = 19.45 - 0.092 = 19.358, which is rounded to the NEAREST 10 mm = 19.36 (a 90 mm fall, not 92 mm). The window then works the grade back from the rounded levels: 9.2 / 0.09 = 102.2, and writes 102 into "Set my own". So the level is rounded to nearest (flatter than 1 in 100), not up. Correction of my earlier note: the "round the fall up to 10 mm" rule belongs to a different path (levels worked out at Start Pipe from the grade); the two paths disagree, which is the real fault (one rule per behaviour). Right answer for 9.2 m at 1 in 100: fall at least 0.092, so downstream 19.35 (or 19.358 shown to 3 decimals), and the grade box stays 100.

**Status:** OPEN (reported by Tim 29 Oct 2026). Never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

## BUG-1231 — EXPLODE of a pit prints a run of repeated "Pit schedule cell for C1 ... not updated" lines about a different item before its one useful sentence

**Command / Area:** EXPLODE on a CE pit (P11, with one pipe) on a drawing that already has a drawn Pit Schedule, Civil 3.0.85 (Tim, by hand on his own PC, 29 Oct 2026, hand check H4). NOISE / WORDING, severity low; the EXPLODE itself worked.

**Symptom:** Tim exploded P11. The command line printed, in order: "1 found", then seven lines "[CE] Pit schedule cell for C1 (outlet pipe size) not updated: the pit or pipe it was placed for no longer matches this drawing's record." and the same for "(inlet from)" and "(inlet pipe size)" (the pair repeated three times), then "[CE] A pit schedule cell whose pit or pipe no longer matches was left as drawn. Run Update existing schedule in PITSCHEDULE to bring the schedule up to date.", and only last the useful line "P11 is now plain linework and has left the schedule; 1 pipe now has an end not connected yet. U restores it." The lines name C1, not P11, so a drafter reads them as a fault in C1.

## BUG-1233 — New Pipe / Edit Pipe silently switches "Pipe grade" from Standard to "Set my own" when it guesses the downstream level

**Command / Area:** CD (New Pipe) and CDEDIT (Edit Pipe) windows, "Pipe grade" choice (Standard / Set my own) with the "I know one end" invert working, Civil 3.0.85 (Tim, by hand on his own PC, 29 Oct 2026). WRONG ANSWER (the window changes your choice without telling you), severity to confirm.

**Symptom:** You draw a pipe and type the upstream level. The window guesses the downstream level, and then the Pipe grade choice switches itself to "Set my own" and fills in a grade number. That is different from Standard, and you did not ask for it. Tim: "i draw a pipe and then i set both upstream and downstream points, after it guessed my downstream it sets the pipe grade to set my own automatically which is different to standard this feature is decieving".
Code reading of the installed build (commit 09126560, not seen live): the step that suggests the downstream level (CdViewModel.Inverts.cs, TryApplyUpstreamDownstreamSuggestion) turns the Standard and Default grade choices off, turns Custom on and writes the worked-back grade number into it. The same step produced the "1 in 102" of BUG-1229 (9.2 m pipe, 90 mm fall).

**Expected behaviour:** The window never changes a choice you made. If Standard was chosen it stays Standard and the guessed downstream level follows it. If a level or grade you typed changes the grade, the window says so in plain words before it switches (for example "This now works out at 1 in 102; keep Standard or use this grade?"). Tim's wording: this is "decieving".

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) CD from P10 to P9, Pipe grade = Standard. (2) Type only the upstream level. (3) Look at the Pipe grade buttons and the grade box. Right = still Standard, no new number in "Set my own", and the downstream level follows Standard. Then type a downstream level by hand: the window may say the grade now differs, but must not switch the choice silently. Repeat in Edit Pipe.

**Reference:** Related BUG-1229 (same step, rounded level and 102), BUG-1230 (on hold) and PC-02 / PC-03 in decisions/2026-10-29_TIM_PLANNING_CHANGES.md (the two-controls problem: the grade row and "I know one end"). Part of the whole-functionality review, but it is a plain wrong answer on its own and Tim reported it as a bug. **Status:** OPEN (reported by Tim 29 Oct 2026). Never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

Any CE drawing command run first (PIT, PIPE, EDIT) makes it right. CDCHECK writes nothing, so the drawing data is not harmed; the check's answer is wrong.

**Cause (from the code and the CE log, NOT yet proven by a run):** CDCHECK reads the pit/pipe record from CE's memory, which still belongs to the closed drawing until a CE drawing command runs; the pipe-to-pit fit check already falls back to the saved list (BUG-589), the connection list does not. Report: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\R21_MOVE_UNDO_DIAGNOSIS_30OCT.md. Not a 3.0.86 regression and not MOVE then U. Related to Tim's BUG-1240 remark ("i always have to cdsync when i reopen drawing").

**Status:** OPEN. Fix job B-055 started 30 Oct 2026 04:37 (CDCHECK reads the list saved in the drawing when none is in memory; switch checks.cdcheckReadsThisDrawingsRecord ON). Never FIXED until Tim confirms in AutoCAD.

## BUG-1252 — A hand-placed pipe label is shifted when its pit moves, with "hand-placed labels stay" ON, and Tidy labels does not count it as hand-placed

**Command / Area:** CE label handling when a pit moves (switch linking.handPlacedLabelsStay ON) and CDTIDYLABELS, Civil 3.0.86 (Codex look G7, 30 Oct 2026 06:27, on a copy; card D13 step 3). Severity to confirm; WRONG ANSWER (label position), not Claude-accepted or Tim-confirmed.

**Symptom:** A 100 mm UPVC pipe from pit P8. The pipe's description was moved up by hand with AutoCAD's MOVE. Then pit P8 was moved sideways 500 mm. The description shifted sideways 250 mm (it stayed above the pipe). Tidy labels then reported "placed by hand: 0". Codex: FAIL, SURE; evidence folder C:\Lisp Files\_TEST_COPIES_20260923\LOOKS\G7_20261030_0627.

**Expected behaviour (the card's wording, D13 step 3):** after you MOVE the description up 1000 mm and then MOVE its pit sideways 500 mm, the label you moved by hand is still exactly where you put it, and Tidy labels counts it as "Placed by hand (left alone) 1".
**Open design question (Tim's Monday question 19, QUESTIONS_FOR_MONDAY.md):** CE's design today is that a label travels with its pipe end when the pit moves. Option (a): keep that and change the card; option (b): build it so a hand-placed label stays put. Recommended (a), because a label left behind ends up detached from its pipe. If Tim chooses (a) this entry becomes a card correction plus a wording fix for Tidy labels; if (b) it is a build item. Note the new result: the label moved HALF the pit's distance (250 mm of 500), which fits neither design.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) Switch ON. Place P8 and a 100 mm pipe; MOVE the pipe description up 1000 mm. (2) MOVE P8 sideways 500 mm. (3) Read the description's position and run Tidy labels. Right (if option b) = description unmoved, Tidy labels says "Placed by hand 1"; right (if option a) = description moved the full 500 mm with the pipe end, never half.

**Reference:** CODEX_VERIFY_G7_20261030_0627.md (G7-01 FAIL), CE 02 message to CE 05 30 Oct 2026. Related BUG-879 (hand-placement marks, another route), robot check N27 (passes only the part it names) and N31, QUESTIONS_FOR_MONDAY.md item 19, CODEX_CASE_REVIEW_cx_cr25.md.


**Cause note (30 Oct 2026, areas/CODEX_BLOCKED_ANALYSIS_30OCT.md (CE 00 Control Room, 30 Oct 2026; read against the source at the installed commit, evidence only, not seen in AutoCAD beyond the Codex looks)):** each pipe label is stored as a segment plus a fraction along the pipe plus an offset (LinkService.SegmentAnalysis.cs, the PipeAttachment builder around lines 260 to 280), so a label near the middle of the pipe moves HALF the pit's move (250 mm of 500). That is the half that fits neither design: it is design (a) with the hand offset kept, anchored mid-pipe. The hand-placed mark (PlacedByHand) is read only by Tidy labels (LinkService.TextClashTidyUp.cs lines 244 to 346); the pit-move re-placement never reads it, so the switch cannot keep a label put. The mark is written only by the atomic attachment move inside a tidy pass, which is why Tidy labels counted zero placed by hand. Also seen: the description re-worded from 1 IN 100 to 1 IN 101 after the move (same family as BUG-357). Stays ON HOLD for Tim's Monday question 19.
**Status:** OPEN - ON HOLD (waits for Tim's answer to Monday question 19: keep or change the label rule). Evidence only; never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) Open the G5 copy (pit P3 with two upper pipe ends). (2) MOVE P3 by 0,2000. (3) Zoom to the pit and read where the upper-left IL text sits against the blue strip. Right = clear of the strip.

**Reference:** CODEX_VERIFY_G5_20261030_0739.md (G5-01), evidence C:\Lisp Files\_TEST_COPIES_20260923\LOOKS\G5_20261030_0739. Related BUG-141 (label tidy) and the Tidy labels family. CE 02 message to CE 05, 30 Oct 2026.


**Cause note (30 Oct 2026, areas/CODEX_BLOCKED_ANALYSIS_30OCT.md (CE 00 Control Room, 30 Oct 2026; read against the source at the installed commit, evidence only, not seen in AutoCAD beyond the Codex looks)):** CE never treats a text's own pipe strip as keep-clear. In LinkService.TextClashTidyUp.cs the pipe, its strip (mline) and its own texts go into ownIds (lines 273 to 286) and the filter skips them as obstacles (lines 687 and 704), so a text on its own pipe strip is never a clash. After a pit move the texts are re-placed by the stored along and offset values on a pipe whose angle changed, and nothing notices the overlap. Seen again independently in the C6-03 look at 08:54. Same root as BUG-1034: fix together.
**Status:** OPEN (evidence from a Codex look, 30 Oct 2026). Never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

## BUG-1255 - Pit Schedule Export Excel fails in AutoCAD 2027: AutoCAD's own older ClosedXML wins over CE's

**Command / Area:** PITSCHEDULE window, Export Excel button, Civil 3.0.86 (Codex look H3, 30 Oct 2026 08:07, on a copy). Severity to confirm; the Codex result is BLOCKED, not a verdict.

**Symptom:** Clicking Export Excel (and one allowed repeat click) opened no file chooser. After the window was closed the command line showed "[CE] Creative Engineering | Pit Schedule rendering error - see CE log for details." twice. No export was made. The CSV export cancel half ran and added no drawing-write line. Codex did not open the CE log, so the cause is unknown; it may be a real fault or a test-set-up fault (the fixture had 27 rows and "95 data issues").

**Expected behaviour:** Export Excel opens the Windows save box, as CSV does. A rendering error line never appears for a normal export.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) Run PITSCHEDULE on a copy with schedule rows. (2) Click Export Excel. (3) Right = the Windows save box opens; read the command line after closing the window for any rendering error. If it repeats, read the CE log line it points at (a robot or desk job; Codex did not).

**Reference:** CODEX_VERIFY_H3_20261030_0807.md (H3-01 BLOCKED), evidence LOOKS\H3_20261030_0807. Related BUG-1198 (cancelling a Pit Schedule export saves the row order), evidence note added there. CE 02 message to CE 05, 30 Oct 2026.


**Cause found (30 Oct 2026, areas/CODEX_BLOCKED_ANALYSIS_30OCT.md (CE 00 Control Room, 30 Oct 2026; read against the source at the installed commit, evidence only, not seen in AutoCAD beyond the Codex looks)):** the CE log (08:13:13 and 08:13:22) shows FileLoadException: could not load ClosedXML 0.102.3.0, thrown at ViewModels/PitScheduleViewModel.Schedule.cs line 113 (ExportExcel). AutoCAD 2027 ships its own older ClosedXML 0.102.2.0 (C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2027\ClosedXML.dll, same publisher key) and it wins over the 0.102.3 that CE Civil and CE Structural reference and ship (CE_CVL_SUITE.csproj line 192, CE_STRUC_SUITE.csproj line 193). Reach: every ClosedXML export in Civil on AutoCAD 2027 (Pit Schedule Excel, likely the CDCALC XLSX export too). Structural's Excel exports very likely fail the same way but this has NOT been seen in AutoCAD: it needs one robot check before it gets its own entry (not filed, to avoid a guess). A second, smaller fault: the window guard turns the crash into "rendering error - see CE log" with no reason for the drafter; a plain line such as "Excel export could not start on this AutoCAD; use Export CSV" is wanted. Fix options for the builder: build the Modern (net10) lane against ClosedXML 0.102.2 to match AutoCAD 2027, or load ClosedXML in CE's own load context; a short accoreconsole probe can show which works. **PILOT-BLOCKER** (lane: 2027; colleagues on 2025 and 2026 not checked). This entry is the bug the analysis calls BUG-1255; no second entry was opened.
**Status:** OPEN - PILOT-BLOCKER (cause found 30 Oct 2026; evidence only). Never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

- Note (trust-safety-fixes, Fri 13 Nov 2026, TRUST-04; nothing installed or accepted): a fix is already in the INSTALLED Civil 3.0.90 (PR #1871: 96b87f73, 9a1f4e64, c137e78a, 0b8698eb, in since 3.0.88), and Codex K1-01 and K1-03 PASSED SURE on 1 Nov on 3.0.88 (save box, two-sheet workbook, opens in Excel). The TRUST-04 card and the 6 Nov audit saying 'no fix exists' are wrong. Cause re-checked on disk 13 Nov: AutoCAD 2027 ships ClosedXML 0.102.2.0, CE references 0.102.3.0. Still owed: K1-04 switch-off look; CDCALC XLSX is BUG-1268. Structural 1.0.126 (8de95c34) does NOT carry the Structural half (9a1f4e64, c137e78a not in it); not seen in AutoCAD. No new branch. Steps: PENDING_TESTS row 4.

## BUG-1267 — New Pipe, "Set my own": typing a new upstream level may carry the OLD fall over to the downstream level (POSSIBLE, found by reading code, not run in AutoCAD)

**Command / Area:** CD (New Pipe window), "Set my own" with remembered levels. Civil. POSSIBLE BUG, UNCONFIRMED. Reported by CE 02 (30 Oct 2026, 23:22) from reading code via CE 00; nothing has been run in AutoCAD. It sits in the same flow as B-057 (#1873) and BUG-1229 and BUG-1233: check whether B-057 already covers it before opening a new build number.

**Symptom (as reported):** Open New Pipe with the previous pipe's levels still remembered (example: upstream 19.00, downstream 18.50). Choose "Set my own" and type a new upstream level 19.45. The old fall (0.50) is carried over, so the downstream fills 18.95. CE 02 expects 19.40: its cases use two pits 4.1 m apart, 100 mm pipe, "Set my own" 1 in 100, so the fall is 4.1 m / 100 = 0.041, rounded up by ApplyCalculatedInvertRule to 0.05, giving 19.45 - 0.05 = 19.40 (CE 02 notes the rounding is to be re-checked, H2). From CE 02, areas/CASE_WRITING_C78_REPORT_30OCT.md (items 7 and 5).

**Expected behaviour:** The downstream is worked out from the grade the drafter chose (1 in 100 over 4.1 m gives 19.40), not from the old pipe's fall. Per CE 02 the code reads the remembered levels through the same setter a drafter uses (CdViewModel.Settings.cs 191-192) and marks the downstream "set by the drafter" (CdViewModel.Inverts.cs 727-731), and ResolveHasEstablishedFall (858-870) counts any chosen grade as an established fall when both old levels are present, so typing 19.45 straight in carries the old fall. Unconfirmed: not run in AutoCAD.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** Open New Pipe so the previous levels (19.00 and 18.50) are remembered, choose "Set my own", and type 19.45 in the upstream box WITHOUT clearing it first. Note the downstream level. The C-78 robot cases clear the upstream box first to avoid this, so a new case must NOT clear it.

**Reference:** CE 02 via CE 00, 30 Oct 2026. Code pointers from CE 02: CdViewModel.Settings.cs lines 191-192, CdViewModel.Inverts.cs lines 727-731 and 858-870. Related: B-057 (#1873), BUG-1229, BUG-1233.

**Status:** OPEN (possible bug, unconfirmed; not reproduced). Never FIXED until confirmed in AutoCAD.

**Evidence note (CE 05, 30 Oct 2026, from CE 01, code read at the C-78 head 7c6af57b; not run, not opened in AutoCAD):** B-057 (#1873) does NOT cover this: it only stops the Grade mismatch window opening on the window's own suggested level (rule MismatchBoxOwnSuggestionRule plus CdCommand.Grade and CdCommand); it does not touch the hold-the-fall logic. Likely cause: "Recall Last" (CdViewModel.Settings.cs 191-192, ApplyStoredSettings) writes the remembered downstream 18.50 through the public SecondInvert setter; that setter (CdViewModel.Inverts.cs 727-731) flips _secondInvertUserSet to true whenever the re-entrancy guard is off, and Recall Last does not switch the guard on; ResolveHasEstablishedFall (858-870) then returns true, so typing a new upstream 19.45 holds the old 0.50 fall (18.95). A recalled level is treated as a fall the drafter set. The hold-the-fall rule is the BUG-076 design (a code comment says it needs Tim's confirmation), so what is right is Tim's call: (a) keep the remembered 0.50 fall (18.95, today) or (b) work from the standard grade for the new upstream (19.40, CE 02's expectation; note CE 02's 19.40 comes from the chosen "Set my own" 1 in 100 over 4.1 m). CE 01 recommends (b) behind a Settings switch ON by default. Question with CE 04. When Tim answers, CE 01 registers one build (next free B-076) together with BUG-1229 and BUG-1233 checks, on the C-79 line. Nothing built until then. Still OPEN, unconfirmed.

Note (CE 05, Sat 31 Oct 2026): Tim answered by voice ("5as recommened", decision item 122): after Recall Last, a new upstream level works from the standard grade for the new pipe's length (19.40 for a 4.1 m pipe at 1 in 100), behind a Settings switch ON; this supersedes the 18.95 behaviour. Job w3 queued for after the 14:00 Team reset (Civil, base rel-20261102a). Still OPEN: not built, not tested in AutoCAD. Separately, decision item 119 (a steeper pipe than the chosen grade also warns) is CE 04's GUESS on Tim's words "2no but warn" and stays UNCONFIRMED; job w1 builds it behind its own switch.

Note (CE 05, Sat 31 Oct 2026): DRAFT PR #1927 (B-095, on the #1919 branch): Recall Last, then a new upstream level, works from the standard grade (19.40 on a 4.1 m pipe at 1 in 100; switch pipe.recallLastNewUpstreamUsesStandardGrade ON). Built and unit-tested only; not opened in AutoCAD. Not fixed.

## BUG-1274 — Pit Schedule leaves plastic pits out and the window does not say so

**Command / Area:** PITSCHEDULE (window, Place schedule), Civil 3.0.90 (commit cf059dcf). Found Wed 4 Nov 2026 on job CG26-20, Dromana, drawing "B FOR COUNCIL APPROVAL_PRE_C7". MEDIUM; WRONG ANSWER by omission (looks like missing pits to the drafter).

The window shows no message that pits were left out. The log shows no error either (13:37:36 gave identities to exactly the five scheduled pits).

**Cause (read from the drawing record and the code, not yet seen in the window):** by the plastic-pit rule (Tim 5 Sep 2026, item 58) a plastic pit is not scheduled unless the drafter uses "Number and schedule this one anyway" in the PIT window. All six have isPlasticPit true, includeInSchedule false, plasticNumberAndScheduleIsManual false, in the 11:39, 13:31 and 13:37 saves. So the schedule is working as ruled; the gap is that nothing tells the drafter.

**Expected behaviour:** when a drawing has pits the schedule leaves out, the Pit Schedule window says how many and why in plain words (for example "6 plastic pits are not in this schedule: P3 to P8. Open PIT on each and press Number and schedule this one anyway to add it."). Same line when the pit is flagged off or marked To be removed. Wording and whether plastic pits should be numbered on the plan at all are for Tim.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** open a drawing with a 350 plastic pit numbered on the plan, run PITSCHEDULE. Right: the window names the pits left out and why. Today: it names nothing.

**Reference:** Modules/Drainage/ViewModels/PitScheduleViewModel.Data.cs (IsEligibleScheduledPit); Rules/PitPresetLocks.cs (CanNumberAndSchedule); Rules/ObjectStatusRule.cs; Dialogs/PitDialog.xaml line 353. Not fix-ready: needs Tim's wording and a decision on plastic pits that carry a number on the plan.

**Status:** OPEN. Logged Wed 4 Nov 2026 by the plugin chat on Tim's yes; nothing built, nothing tested.

## BUG-1282 — CD: reports success when a label, level text or arrow could not be made, and the record says it exists

**Command / Area:** CD (New Pipe), pipe text, invert (level) text and flow arrow creation. MEDIUM. WRONG ANSWER (record out of step with the drawing).

**Symptom:** If creating the pipe label, a level text or the arrow fails, CD only writes the failure to the CE log. The drafter sees no warning. The schedule record is written with the requested flags (first and second level shown, label made), so the record says the label exists when the drawing has none. Only a missing MLINE border gets an on-screen warning.

**Expected behaviour:** A failed label, level text or arrow prints one plain line naming which one is missing, and the record does not claim it exists (it stays Unknown or is marked missing).

## BUG-1286 — Fifteen tools have no start-up checks (read-only drawing, Paper Space, REFEDIT, Structural drawing)

**Command / Area:** CDCALC, CDDEST, CDMA, CDMANAGER, CDRAINFALL, CDREVERSEFLOW, CDRULEBOOK, CDRULES, CDSYSTEM, CDTEXTSEG, CDTIDYLABELS, CDTWL, CR, MR and PITSCHEDULE. MEDIUM. MISSING PROTECTION.

## BUG-1361 — STRSCHEDSYNC with no edits turns every rotated brace again and rewrites every brace's length and angle

**Command / Area:** STRSCHEDSYNC (Schedules, sync the bracing table back to the drawing). HIGH. WRONG ANSWER, silent change to bracing on the drawing. Engineering judgement: Tim.

**Symptom:** The bracing table's ROTATION column shows the block's own rotation setting, which is zero for a brace the drafter turned with AutoCAD ROTATE, so the table then shows the object's turn instead. STRSCHEDSYNC reads every row back and writes each row's length and rotation into the brace block again, even when nobody edited the table. A ROTATEd brace gets its angle applied a second time, so it turns again. Every brace's length and angle is also rewritten at the table's two-decimal rounding (a 2699.996 mm brace becomes 2700, an angle of 89.9973 becomes 90). The drafter sees braces move or change length after a sync they did only to push one typed edit.

**Expected behaviour:** A sync changes only the cells the drafter edited. A brace the drafter turned with ROTATE is never turned again, and lengths and angles that were not edited keep their exact stored values.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) On a copy, place two AB braces and ROTATE one of them 30 degrees. (2) Run STRSCHEDCREATE and note the table. (3) Note each brace's length and angle with LIST or Properties. (4) Run STRSCHEDSYNC on the bracing table without editing any cell. (5) Compare both braces to step 3. Right = both identical to step 3. Wrong = the turned brace is now at a different angle, or a length or angle changed in the third decimal.

**Test that catches it:** Fixture: a bracing table built from a drawing with one ROTATEd brace; run the sync with no cell edits; assert every brace's length, rotation and position equal their values before the sync. Unit: a cell whose text equals the rounded stored value is not written back.

**Reference:** Services\ScheduleService.cs:409-410 (table cells written at two decimals) and 725-756 (SyncBracingTable writes length and rotation for every row, no change test); Services\ProjectDataService.cs:322-326 (rotation falls back to br.Rotation when the dynamic value is under 0.0001). Already named in the hunt note as BRACE-01 with no bug number. Installed Structural 1.0.126 (commit 8de95c34), read in the code copy C:\CE_WORK\scratch\audit_struc, paths under Modules\Structural unless stated. Source: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\trust-run\STRUCTURAL_NEW_FAULTS_TO_FILE.md.

**Evidence:** Found by reading the installed code on 13 Nov 2026. Not yet seen in AutoCAD.

**Note 2026-11-13 04:19 (lane trust-struc-mgr-plan, after review `areas\trust-run\reviews\structural-tool-notes-sample.md`; status unchanged):** the trigger is narrower than the title. AB and BB draw a brace with the block turned 0 and the angle in the brace's own turning value (`Services\BracingService.cs:1677-1681, 1706-1708`). So only a brace drawn flat (within 1 degree, or the Enter default) and later turned with AutoCAD ROTATE gets its angle applied a second time, and only on the first sync. A brace drawn at an angle and then turned shows the wrong angle in the table, but sync writes the same value back and nothing moves. The two-decimal rewrite of every length and angle is real and small. Steps to confirm: draw the brace flat (Enter at the angle), then ROTATE it 30 degrees.

**Note 2026-11-13 (lane trust-core-ribbon):** draft fix in pull request 2071 (branch `claude/trust-b1361-sync-changes-nothing`): the sync writes only the cells the drafter edited; an unedited cell (its text equals what the table shows for the brace now) is left alone, so nothing is turned again and no length or angle is rewritten at table rounding. Built and unit-tested only; not seen in AutoCAD; assumptions for Tim are in the pull request (what an edited ROTATION cell should mean for a brace turned with ROTATE is not decided). Status unchanged.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1362 — ABS (A-B switch) erases an older brace first, and if the new one cannot be drawn says "It was left as it was"

**Command / Area:** ABSWITCH (Structural A-B bracing switch), older-named brace blocks ("A - BRACING LEFT" and the like). HIGH. WRONG ANSWER, lost brace with a false message. Engineering judgement: Tim.

**Symptom:** When ABS converts an older brace block to the new BRACING block it erases the old block, then tries to draw the new one. If the new block cannot be drawn (block missing, layer problem, insert fails) the brace is gone, but the command line says "Could not convert one older bracing block. It was left as it was." The drafter loses a brace from the wall and is told it is still there. Bracing totals then fall short with no warning.

**Expected behaviour:** The old brace is erased only after the new one is drawn. If the new one cannot be drawn the old brace stays exactly as it was and the line says so truthfully. Undo puts back what the command did.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) On a copy place an older-named brace block ("A - BRACING LEFT") on a wall line and note it. (2) Make the new BRACING block unavailable (rename it in the Block Editor on the copy, or lock the target brace layer so the insert fails). (3) Run ABS and pick the old brace. (4) Look at the line and the drawing. Right = the old brace is still there and unchanged. Wrong = the brace has gone while the line says it was left as it was.

**Test that catches it:** Fixture: older-named brace plus a failing InsertBracingBlock; assert the old block is not erased when the insert fails and the message does not claim it was kept unless it is present.

**Reference:** Services\BracingService.cs:2169-2191 (ConvertLegacyToNew erases at 2171-2172, inserts at 2176, returns false at 2190-2191); Commands\BracingCommands.cs:395-398 and 496-499 (message). Related BUG-583 (locked brace, unhandled error). Installed Structural 1.0.126 (commit 8de95c34), read in the code copy C:\CE_WORK\scratch\audit_struc, paths under Modules\Structural unless stated. Source: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\trust-run\STRUCTURAL_NEW_FAULTS_TO_FILE.md.

**Evidence:** Found by reading the installed code on 13 Nov 2026. Not yet seen in AutoCAD.

**Note 2026-11-13 04:19 (lane trust-struc-mgr-plan, after review `areas\trust-run\reviews\structural-tool-notes-sample.md`; status unchanged):** the trigger is narrower than the title. The brace is lost only when the BRACING block cannot be loaded: ABS then only warns and carries on (`Commands\BracingCommands.cs:395-398`), erases the old brace and keeps that change (`Services\BracingService.cs:2169-2174`), the insert fails with "Block 'BRACING' not found" (1670-1673), and the line still says it was left as it was (`BracingCommands.cs:496-499`). A locked target layer is refused earlier and does not trigger it, so step 2's "lock the target brace layer" will not show the fault; make the BRACING block unavailable instead. One U brings the brace back.

**Note 2026-11-13 (lane trust-core-ribbon):** draft fix in pull request 2068 (branch `claude/trust-b1362-abs-keeps-brace`): the new brace is drawn first and the older one erased last; if the older one cannot be erased the new one is taken back out. Built and unit-tested only (3 of 4 new tests fail on the installed code); not seen in AutoCAD. Status unchanged.

## BUG-1363 — A schedule size the support block cannot show is drawn as the default size while the screen line names the schedule size

**Command / Area:** C1, C2, DS, DS1, TS1 (support blocks). HIGH. WRONG ANSWER, size on the drawing differs from the schedule. Engineering judgement: Tim.

**Symptom:** When the member schedule gives a size the block has no state for (a timber stud pack such as "2 No 90 x 45 F17 KDHW", or a steel size the block lacks), the command still prints "[CE] DS1: size 'X' from the schedule, shown as 'Y'". Wrong = the line says the schedule size and the block shows the default.

**Test that catches it:** Fixture: schedule row with a non-steel size; run the visibility step; assert the message names the fallback when the requested state is not offered. Unit: SetDynamicVisibility returns a distinct result when it used the fallback.

## BUG-1456 — Help (CDHELP) or Settings (CDS) run first in a second drawing writes the FIRST drawing's pits and pipes into it

**Command / Area:** CDHELP and CDS, Civil 3.0.90 (commit cf059dcf), AutoCAD 2027. HIGH; DATA: one job's stored CE data is overwritten by another job's, with nothing on screen. Found Fri 13 Nov 2026: first by a reviewer reading the code, then SEEN by the robot in real AutoCAD on the installed build, on copies only, 6 times in 11 tries, in both directions. Evidence: `areas\trust-run\EVIDENCE_CROSS_DRAWING.md`. Not Codex-looked, not seen by Tim.

**Symptom:** work in job A (any CE command run there, so CE holds A's record in memory). Open or switch to drawing B. As the very first thing in B, run Help (CDHELP) or Settings (CDS) and close the window. B's stored CE record is now A's. Seen: a blank drawing with no CE data gained 11 pits and 49 pipes and its changed counter went from 0 to 1 (so it asks "save changes?"); a different job holding 2 pits and 46 pipes was overwritten with the first job's 11 and 49; and the other way round the first job was overwritten with the second job's 2 and 46. Nothing is printed. The drafter sees a normal Help or Settings window.

**When it does NOT happen (seen):** when any plain AutoCAD command (a circle, then U) was run in the second drawing first; and in one run after a cancelled PIT and a cancelled CD. Two copies of the same job hide it, because the wrong record looks the same.

**Expected behaviour:** Help and Settings never write to any drawing. No CE command ever writes one drawing's record into another.

**Cause (read from the code, consistent with what was seen):** CDHELP and CDS are on the list of commands whose end saves CE's stored record even when nothing is waiting, and they never attach the record to the current drawing first, so the record still in memory from the previous drawing is written into the current one. Same family as BUG-385, BUG-378 and BUG-1225.

**Until it is fixed, the safe habit:** in a drawing you have just opened or switched to, do not make Help or Settings the first CE thing you run; and if a drawing you did not edit asks to save, answer No.

**Fix in progress (not installed, not accepted):** draft pull request 2064 (`claude/trust-09-cancel-writes-nothing`, switch off by default): a command that never attached the record to the current drawing never writes; a cancelled command writes nothing.

**A test that catches it:** two different made-up jobs; run a CE command in the first; make the second current; run CDHELP and close; the second drawing's stored record and changed counter must be exactly as before. Repeat with CDS, with a blank drawing, and in the other order. A deliberately faulty version that writes must fail.

**Steps to confirm the fix in AutoCAD:** (1) open test job A and run CDDIAG; (2) open test job B, which has different pits; (3) straight away type CDHELP, close the window; (4) open the Pit Schedule in B: right = B's own pits, not A's; (5) open a blank drawing, type CDS, close it, then close the drawing: right = no "save changes?" question. Not yet known: what a later tool does with the wrong record, and what happens if the contaminated drawing is saved (the robot never saved).

**Status:** OPEN. Found by test on the installed build 13 Nov 2026.


## BUG-1457 — CLEAN and FASTSAVE in a drawing that has never been saved save straight over the template file it was made from

**Command / Area:** CLEAN and FASTSAVE, Structural 1.0.126 (commit 8de95c34), AutoCAD 2027. HIGH; DATA: an office template can be overwritten, so every later drawing made from it starts with that job's content. SEEN in real AutoCAD by the robot on the installed build, on a scratch copy of AutoCAD's own metric template only. Evidence: `areas\trust-run\EVIDENCE_CLEAN_TEMPLATE.md`. Not Codex-looked, not seen by Tim. Earlier listed as "not confirmed, needs a robot probe" in `areas\trust-run\STRUCTURAL_FAULTS_NOT_CONFIRMED.md`; the probe has now confirmed it.

**Symptom:** the drafter starts a new drawing from a template (it is still called Drawing1 and has never been saved) and runs CLEAN or FASTSAVE before using Save As. Nothing is asked. The command says it saved, the drawing is renamed after the template file, and the template file now holds that drawing. Seen: CLEAN took a template copy from 31,825 to 33,398 bytes; FASTSAVE took another copy from 31,825 to 32,022 bytes (fingerprints changed). FASTSAVE printed "saved <template name>.dwt". The next new drawing made from that template starts with the job's content.

**Expected behaviour:** in a drawing that has never been saved, CLEAN and FASTSAVE do not save. They say "Save the drawing with a name first" and stop (the clean-up part may still run), or open AutoCAD's own Save As. They never write to a template file.

**Cause (from the code, consistent with what was seen; the run did not trace it further):** `CleanPipelineService` runs its QSave stage through CE's managed save, `DrawingAutoSaveService.TrySaveNow`; for an unnamed drawing that save takes the drawing's template file as its name and `DrawingAutoSaveService.cs:198` calls `db.SaveAs(drawingPath, ...)` on it. `DrawingSafetyService.TryGetNormalProjectDrawing` only refuses the `.sv$` and `.ac$` autosave names, so nothing stops it. AutoCAD's own QSAVE would have asked for a name.

**Until it is fixed, the safe habit:** save a new drawing with its own name before running CLEAN or FASTSAVE.

**A test that catches it:** a made-up template file; start a new drawing from it (never saved); run CLEAN; the template file's size, date and fingerprint must be exactly as before and the drawing must still be unnamed. Repeat with FASTSAVE. Also run both after Save As with a real name: they must save into that file. A deliberately faulty version that saves to the template must fail.

**Steps to confirm the fix in AutoCAD, on a COPY of a template only (never the office template):** (1) copy a template to a scratch folder and note its size and date; (2) start a new drawing from the copy and draw one line, do not save; (3) type CLEAN: right = a plain line saying to save with a name first (or AutoCAD's Save As opens), the title bar still says Drawing1; (4) repeat with FASTSAVE; (5) check the template copy: right = same size and date as in step 1; (6) now Save As with a real name and run CLEAN and FASTSAVE: right = both save into that file.

**Note 2026-11-13 (lane trust-core-ribbon):** draft fix in pull request 2094: CLEAN and FASTSAVE stop first, with one plain line, in a never-saved drawing or one whose file is a template; the managed save, both CLEAN save stages and the sheet sync write refuse a template. Built and unit-tested only; the fault was seen in AutoCAD, the fix has not been. Status unchanged.

**Status:** OPEN. Seen on the installed build, 13 Nov 2026, on a template copy; Tim's real template untouched (same hash).

## BUG-1458 — PIT: Esc at the first point still leaves CE's record update in the drawing (blank pit inverts filled from the pipes)

**Command / Area:** PIT (New Pit). MEDIUM. UNEXPECTED STORED-DATA CHANGE.

**Symptom:** Before PIT asks for the insertion point, it brings CE's whole record up to date with the drawing (`EnsureDrawingDataCurrent`). That update is not held. Its last step fills every blank pit invert from the lowest connected pipe end, and it is saved into the drawing at once. Pressing Esc at "pick the insertion point" ends PIT with "PIT command cancelled.", but the filled pit inverts (and anything else the update changed) stay in CE's record. Only U takes them back. This is the same kind of fault as CDEDIT's (queue item 27, batch 11 item 19: "CE updated its record (CDEDIT): 2 pit invert levels filled in." stayed after Cancel) and as BUG-1285 (CDTG, CDSL, CDWT).

**Expected behaviour:** Esc at PIT's first prompt (or Cancel in its window) leaves CE's record byte-equal to before and prints no "CE updated its record" line. Any update PIT needs is written only with a placed pit, in the same single Undo. This is the same hold Edit Pipe, CDRUNSOLVE and CDPROPAGATE use (BUG-373, BUG-290), and CDEDIT with trust.cdeditCancelWritesNothing on. Whether a pit invert should be filled from the pipes at all is Tim's call (queue item 27): it is a level CE writes by itself.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) On a copy: pits P1 and P2 with cover levels and no inverts, one pipe P1 to P2 with levels 19.20 and 19.10. Save and note CE's record length. (2) Type PIT and press Esc at the insertion point. (3) Save and read CE's record. Right = record identical, P1 and P2 inverts still blank, no "CE updated its record" line. Wrong = P1 19.200 and P2 19.100 filled in, record longer.

**Test that catches it:** Source guard: PIT's record update before its first prompt runs under a record-write hold, which is accepted only when a pit is placed. Fixture: a record with blank pit inverts and known pipe ends; open the hold, run the update, cancel; the in-memory record equals the copy taken before.

**Reference:** Modules\Drainage\Commands\PitCommand.cs:111 (`EnsureDrawingDataCurrent` before `AskPitInsertionPoint` at :115, unheld); Services\ProjectDataService.cs `EnsureDrawingDataCurrent` (ends with `DeriveMissingPitInvertsFromPipes`, BUG-605); Services\ProjectDataService.RecordWriteHold.cs (the hold). Not fixed (controller, 16 Nov: "note it in the carpark as its own bug ... Do not fix yet").

## BUG-1459 — A CE pipe shows nothing in AutoCAD without CE (the picture saved in the drawing is empty)

**Command / Area:** CE pipe object (CE_CVL_OBJECTS_2027.dbx), every drawing with a CE pipe sent to someone without CE. HIGH. DRAWING SENT OUT LOOKS INCOMPLETE.

**Symptom:** Tim, 16 Nov 2026 (relayed by the controller): "projects that used the current or close to current version that use the new pipe type and it doesnt show for people who dont have the plugin". Measured headless on a drawing saved by Civil 3.0.90.13 and opened with no CE: the pipe is a view-only object (ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY), PROXYGRAPHICS 1, PROXYSHOW 1, and EXPLODE of it leaves nothing. CE's ProxyGraphicsGuard only sets PROXYGRAPHICS; nothing ever checked the picture itself.

**Cause:** CeCvlPipeObject derives from AcDbPolyline. The ObjectARX reference for AcDbPolyline::saveAs says a class derived from it must provide its own saveAs, "If such classes do not provide their own implementation of saveAs(), then no graphics will be saved as proxies." It had none. Single and twin pipes alike (one class). The older CeCvlPipe (AcDbCurve) uses AutoCAD's default and never had the gap.

**Expected behaviour:** a drawing saved with CE opens without CE showing each pipe as on screen (dashed band per barrel and magenta walls), view only.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) In a scratch copy draw a pipe and a twin pipe with CD, save, close. (2) Open it with CE not loaded. Right = both pipes show. Wrong = nothing where the pipes are. (3) A drawing saved by 3.0.90.13: open with the fixed version, QSAVE, open without CE: the pipe shows.

**Test that catches it:** Bug1459ProxyPictureSavedTests (source guards: the pipe object declares saveAs and saves worldDraw for every save type). Headless proof: open with no CE and EXPLODE the view-only object; real linework must appear (C:\CE_WORK\scratch\proxy13\px13_run.ps1).

**Reference:** Modules\Drainage.NativeObjects2027\CeCvlPipeObject.h/.cpp (saveAs). Draft PR 2112 (claude/trust-bug1459-proxy-picture); build branch claude/trust-proxy-picture-saveas; batch 13 (Civil 3.0.90.15+2c8b7b1a, prepared, not installed). Also proven: a pipe drawn by the Civil plugin the CD way (harness UX-MIX-01, 16 Nov 14:22) explodes without CE into the band and two walls. Runbook: areas\trust-run\INSTALL_BATCH_14NOV.md, BATCH 13.

**Evidence:** Headless (AutoCAD 2027 core console, 16 Nov 13:14, lane trust-safety-fixes). Saved by the batch 11 enabler, EXPLODE without CE left 0 entities: fresh single+twin, and the robot's 3.0.90.13 drawing. Saved by the batch 13 enabler: 9 polylines for single+twin, and 3 for the robot's drawing after one SAVEAS or QSAVE. Not yet seen in GUI AutoCAD or on a PC without CE.

**Status:** OPEN (fix built in batch 13, not installed)

## BUG-1460 — EXPLODE of a CE pipe erases its label, invert texts and flow arrow

**Command / Area:** EXPLODE / BURST of a CE pipe (CE's erase clean-up at command end). MEDIUM. DRAWING CONTENT LOST ON A NORMAL AUTOCAD COMMAND.

**Symptom:** Tim, 16 Nov 2026 (relayed by the controller): "CURRENTLY I EXPLODE AND IT REMOVES ALL TEXT, ARROW AND JUST KEEPS TWO POLYLINES AND THEN THE CENTEAL POLYLINE WHICH IS NOT EXACTLY EHAT I ASKED FOR", and "INVERTS STAY AS WELL YEAH?".

**Cause:** at the end of every command that erases a CE pipe, LinkService.Compound.cs CascadeErasePipeCompound erases everything on the pipe's own list with it: the pipe label, the first-point and last-point invert texts, the flow arrow and any supplementary text. EXPLODE erases the pipe (AutoCAD puts its pieces in its place), so it was treated as a deleted pipe. Pit-owned texts sit on the pit's own list and were never affected.

**Expected behaviour (Tim's choice A, confirmed):** EXPLODE of a CE pipe leaves the wall lines, the centre band as drawn, the pipe label, the invert texts and the flow arrow, all as ordinary objects. Nothing else changes. ERASE unchanged; one U restores everything.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) Scratch copy: EXPLODE one CE pipe. Right = label, both ILs and arrow stay; pits and their texts untouched. (2) U once: pipe back whole. (3) ERASE another pipe: its label, ILs and arrow go with it.

**Test that catches it:** Bug1460ExplodeKeepsPipeAnnotationTests (19). Headless harness checks XK-01, XK-U-01 and XK-ERASE-01 (Modules\Drainage.HeadlessProof\ExplodeKeepChecks.cs).

**Reference:** Modules\Drainage\Services\LinkService.Compound.cs (CascadeErasePipeCompound, ReleaseFromErasedPipe); LinkService.Utilities.cs (ProcessPendingErasures); ExplodeKeepsPipeAnnotationPolicy.cs; Settings linking.explodeKeepsPipeAnnotation (default on). Draft PR 2112; batch 13 (Civil 3.0.90.15+2c8b7b1a, prepared, not installed).

**Evidence:** Headless harness on the batch 13 payload, 16 Nov 14:20-14:22: XK-01 PASS (label "225 DIA. UPVC PIPE AT 1 IN 100", "IL 10.00", "IL 9.80" and arrow TIM_CVL_ARROW kept and unlinked; band and 2 walls from the explode; nothing else erased), XK-U-01 PASS, XK-ERASE-01 PASS. Not yet seen in GUI AutoCAD.

**Status:** OPEN (fix built in batch 13, not installed)

**Title:** Native hatch: some boundary edges cannot be selected by grip, and "recreate boundary" gives separate polylines instead of one joined polyline

**Command / Area:** AutoCAD's own HATCH grips and Recreate Boundary (HATCHEDIT), on Tim's working PC with the CE plug-ins installed. Not a CE command. Lane: 2027.

**Symptom:** (WRONG BEHAVIOUR of a native tool; severity: slows everyday drafting.) SEE HOW I CANT SELECT SOME EDGES, ALSO WHEN I RECREATE BOUNDARY IT CREATES INDIVIDUAL POLYLINES AS OPPOSED TO JOINED ONES. THIS IS SOMETHING WITH THE GRIP ISSUES." **Expected behaviour:** Native hatches behave exactly as plain AutoCAD: every boundary edge and vertex has its grip, and Recreate Boundary gives one joined polyline for a boundary that was one closed loop. Loading a CE plug-in must change nothing about a native hatch, polyline or block.

**Steps to confirm in AutoCAD:** (1) In a new drawing from the office template, draw a closed polyline with one arc segment, hatch it, delete the boundary, select the hatch: every edge and vertex should show a grip. (2) Recreate boundary as a polyline: one closed polyline should result. (3) Repeat on the hatch Tim photographed. A way of telling "the plug-in" from "AutoCAD itself" is being written: see Reference.

**Test that catches it:** none yet. Wanted: hatch boundary grips and Recreate Boundary compared with and without the CE plug-ins loaded, identical.

**Reference:** Zero-plan decision D-199 (`C:\CE_PLAN\zero\DECISIONS.md`); research in progress, `C:\CE_PLAN\zero\reference\research\R-006_HATCH_AND_GRIPS.md` (reads the installed plug-ins' grip and overrule code read-only, and Autodesk's own pages). Installed versions at the time: not read. Related by subject only, not duplicates: the CEHATCH entries (CE's own hatch command).

**Evidence:** Tim's screenshot of 18 Nov 2026 (in the zero-plan chat). No test run.

**Status:** OPEN

## BUG-1462 — Team and Codex test runs start inside AutoCAD work hours and slow Tim's PC

**Command / Area:** Not a plugin command. The test robots: the Claude "team" run (`team_run.sh`, working copy `C:\CE_WORK\team_a`) and the Codex review run (`codex exec` in `C:\CE_WORK\codex_test`). MEDIUM. SLOWS TIM'S DRAFTING.

**Symptom:** Tim, Thu 19 Nov 2026, about 11:15am, in a general chat: "compuiter is running slow, how come can you fix?". AutoCAD was open (started 09:28) and lagging.

**Cause (measured 11:20 to 11:25am, read from the running programs, not assumed):** every processor thread was busy (processor utility 112 to 152% over five one-second samples, 20 threads). Five copies of `CeCivil.Bench.exe` were running at once, with their compilers and test hosts. Their parent programs: `team_run.sh opus` started 11:00 (check_detention4), and two `codex exec` runs in `C:\CE_WORK\codex_test` started 11:00 and 11:22 (review_G r4). Memory (17.5 of 64 GB free) and disk were fine. This is inside the in-use window of RULES 1.8 (8:30am to 2:00pm): "Big builds and automated testing go in the free windows."

**Not known:** whether these runs were started under a written exception (for example the release charter or a pilot). Not checked by the logging chat. If one applies, say so here and treat this as a request to make the runs gentler on the PC instead.

**Expected behaviour:** in the in-use windows (weekdays 8:30am to 2:00pm and 3:00pm to 5:30pm) no robot starts a build or a test run that loads the processor while Tim's AutoCAD is open; or, if a written exception allows it, the run is held to a small share of the processor (low priority and a cap on how many run at once) so AutoCAD does not lag.

**Steps to confirm:** on a weekday between 9am and 1pm with Tim's AutoCAD open, open Task Manager, Details tab, sort by CPU. Right = no `CeCivil.Bench.exe`, `testhost.exe` or `VBCSCompiler.exe` near the top, and total CPU well under half. Wrong = several of them at once and CPU near 100%.

**Test that catches it:** none yet. Wanted: the run launchers (`team_run.sh` and the Codex start script) refuse or wait when the clock is inside the in-use window and `acad.exe` is running, and log that they waited.

**Reference:** RULES 1.8 and ROUTER step 6 (`C:\TimOS`); `C:\CE_PLAN\desk_jobs\` (launchers and occupancy log; not read by the logging chat).

**Evidence:** process list and parent chains read on Tim's PC, 19 Nov 2026 11:22 to 11:25. Stop-gap applied on Tim's word ("Yes, AutoCAD first"): the running AutoCAD (pid 206484) was set to Above normal priority, read back as set; it lasts only until that AutoCAD closes. No robot run was stopped. Whether AutoCAD felt faster afterwards: not reported.

**Status:** OPEN

- Note (general chat, Thu 19 Nov 2026, BUG-1462): Tim, same day, after this entry was logged: "somedays i might not be in the foffice so test runs can happen". Interpretation (the logging chat's, not Tim's words): the measure is whether Tim is working at this PC, not the clock alone. On a day he is out of the office, robot builds and test runs may run in work hours. On a day he is in and his AutoCAD is open, they wait or run gently. How a launcher is to know he is away (for example the TIM_AWAY flag in desk_jobs) was not said and not checked.
